NEXT: (1) finish W45978 critique (two isolated assessments in flight), then the remaining six root/app pages with a slop row: plant-connections, public-feed, resume, shift-brain, status, voice-journal. (2) THE BOTTOM-CHROME STACK is now a named unit with its measurements: five pieces of chrome anchor to the bottom edge by their own literals (#wh-hub 80px up, learn-link's guide chip ~193px in the degraded state, #wh-connection-notice at 232px, #wh-update-notice, #wh-ai-widget) and any two showing at once push the stack over content - it has covered a control on TWO pages now (marketplace-seller's #ps-gap-retry W45961, ph-intelligence's help disclosure W45975). ## §W3 · EXPANSION WAVE 3 — the FULL-JOURNEY wave, and the eight measured gaps beside it (Ian, 2026-09-07)

Ian: *"let us now extend the numbers of our trajectories, I want you to determine first"* -> *"add also the
trajectories for full journeys, diverse, for my platform"* -> *"we still have to expand and extend the
journeys."* So the wave was **determined before it was designed**: every count below is a gap measured in
the registry as it stood at the close of wave 2, and the largest direction is the one the program was
thinnest on.

### What the determination found (measured read-only, 2026-09-07)

| Axis | What 2,437 rows actually held |
|---|---|
| **Whole journeys barely existed** | **9 rows crossed >=3 pages and none crossed five.** 171 rows used journey words; 117 of them walked a single page. |
| **Cast in the wrong verticals** | The platform hosts **Manila Electronics Assembly, Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg., Baguio Textile Mills, Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, Ramos Jeepney Line, Tan Delivery Vans** - and the registry held 1 electronics row, 0 textile, a few pharma, against 307 vehicle and 37 power-plant rows. |
| **Content pages had one row each** | 54 learn articles: 1 row apiece, all Usability; **52 with zero F, A and I.** 60 calculators: 47 at one row; **59 lacking F, 59 lacking A, 60 lacking I.** |
| **The critic had graded them once** | 31 root pages on the full rubric; **146 pages on a single dimension** (CV1, anon CTA activation): 53 learn, 47 calculators, 48 function files. |
| **Edge functions** | 6 with no row at all, 56 with exactly one. |
| **Shared components** | 17 root scripts named in no row - `connectivity-widget.js` ships on 33 pages. |
| **Cells never walked** | Per root page: new-user 18 · returner 18 · tablet-768 18 · deep-link 18 · anon 27 · search-arrival 37 · qr-print 33 missing. 102 of 546 page x layer cells empty. |
| **Lifecycle lenses** | mic/camera denied 1 · second hive 7 · year-2 aging 10 · leaving 10 · two tabs 21 · export->import 23 · notification storm 25 · release skew 30. |

### The nine directions, and the honest arithmetic

**1,502 new rows seeded in one change: 2,437 -> 3,939 in scope, and the headline dropped to 61.9% the same
day** - the same discipline as every prior wave (the denominator moves once; the generator does the
arithmetic; a hand-typed number fails the `trajectory-registry` gate).

| Code | Direction | Rows | How the count was derived |
|---|---|---|---|
| **W3-JN** | **Full diverse journeys** | **724** | 32 archetypes x the platform's own cast x four tiers (below) |
| W3-LN | Learn articles to full UFAI | 156 | one row per missing dimension per article |
| W3-CL | Calculators to full UFAI | 178 | one row per missing dimension per calculator |
| W3-FN | Edge-function contracts | 186 | 62 functions x refusal / degradation / documented job |
| W3-SC | Shared components as subjects | 56 | 14 scripts x four UFAI lenses, each on three host pages |
| W3-PG | Persona · device · entry gaps | 55 | the cells a root page had never been walked in |
| W3-LC | Lifecycle lenses | 64 | 8 thin shapes x 8 surfaces each |
| W3-AR | Empty page x layer cells | 79 | one row per empty (page, layer) where the layer applies |
| W3-DF | Wave-2 deferred carry-over | 4 | what the last wave found and named as deferred |

The plan estimated ~1,539; the seeder **measured** 1,502. The difference is where an estimate met the
registry: the persona-gap roster came out at 55 rather than 129 because arrival cells that only ever reach
a sign-in door were excluded (the deep-link lens that once graded the same door 24 times), and the empty
page x layer roster came out at 79 rather than 60. `tools/seed_expansion_wave3.py` is the one place that
decides the size, and `validate_trajectory_registry.py` derives its expected ids from it.

### W3-JN - what a journey row is

One whole story: a named person (or a **role pair**, because a two-sided journey owes one side each), cast
in one of the six hives or as a hive-less operator or an anonymous arrival; a device, a language, a moment
in the hive's life, and a condition. It crosses **>=4 pages and >=3 layers**; tier D crosses **>=8 pages,
>=5 layers and three moments**.

| Tier | What varies | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| **A** base cast | every archetype x every vertical it applies to · phone · English · today | **130** |
| **B** device + language | each again on a desktop, and Filipino-first on both devices | **381** |
| **C** overlays | condition x3, moment x2, entry x2, assistive x2, tablet/kiosk | **197** |
| **D** whole lifetimes | a hive's year, a worker's career, a machine's life, a part, a listing, a project, a vehicle | **16** |

The 32 archetypes span the platform's own stages: **acquire** (onboard to first value, alone-then-not,
stranger-to-member, new hire, locked out) · **operate** (breakdown to close-out, the PM month, the
AI-assisted day, the supervisor's week, two hives one person, safety incident, one spare part, the brief
arrives) · **maintain** (sensor to work order, predicted risk, one machine's life, the energy audit, an
engineering project, typhoon season) · **comply** (audit season, the founder's month-end, benchmark to
decision) · **trade** (shortage to shelf, hire a specialist, a deal goes wrong, money in and spent) ·
**grow** (the knowledge loop, the portable portfolio) · **integrate** (the machine client, the vehicle
owner's month) · **degrade** (the same day degraded, leaving).

### The instrument, and the three faults it had before it had any findings

`tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs` walks each story's ordered path in one context and grades three rails: the
**transition** (the next surface is reachable from this one and arrives as itself - never that a control was
clickable), the **identity** (hive, role and name survive every hop), and the **effect** (each archetype
declares a JOIN along its own chain, read *as the person*, so a chain proven only by both ends existing is
not proven).

Its first run reported six failures out of six, and **all three causes were the instrument**:

1. **The nav hub is a closed drawer, and a closed drawer is not an absent one.** The hub is
   `visibility:hidden` until opened, so a visibility filter across the page read *"no way onward at all"* on
   every hop of every journey. A hub link now counts whether or not the drawer is open; only the page's own
   links must be on screen to count as its own thread.
2. **A thread read on a page you did not ask for is not that page's thread.** Three fleet casts could not
   sign in, every step bounced to `index.html`, and the walk cheerfully counted the landing page's links as
   five journey threads - the deep-link lens grading the sign-in door, one layer along. A step that did not
   arrive now contributes no thread evidence at all.
3. **The platform's own table, not mine.** The chain for the breakdown journey counted `anomaly_alerts`,
   which holds zero rows in every hive; `alert-hub.html` reads **`v_alert_truth`**. Six hives whose alert
   page renders a full screen were reported as *"the chain is empty here."*

And one real setup gap: the three fleet accounts had no recoverable password, so the fleet journeys could
not be walked as authenticated people at all. Their local fixtures were given the same test credential the
plant hives already use - a local, reversible seed change, made rather than spoofing a session, because a
walk that fakes its identity is the *probe's-persona-was-an-admin* failure in a new costume.

### Three of the six hives could not LIVE the stories, and that is a seeding job

The first J2 walk ("breakdown to diagnose to close-out") found the plant hives whole - six of six steps
arriving, the identity held across every hop, the chain reading 27 to 36 rows as the person - and the three
fleet hives **empty**: Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, Ramos Jeepney Line and Tan Delivery Vans held vehicles and
**zero logbook entries**. They were seeded as a vehicle registry, never as an operating fleet, so more than
twenty archetypes had nothing to be true about in half the platform's own verticals.

Missing data is a seeding job, never a blocker. `tools/seed_fleet_history.py` writes eight believable jobs
per fleet - oil changes, brake pads, an alternator that stopped charging mid-route, an LTO roadworthiness
pre-check - **against the units each fleet already owns** (a 2026 Ford Ranger XLT, a 2023 Toyota HiAce
Commuter, a 2019 Nissan LEAF), reported by that fleet's own supervisor, every row marked and reversible with
`--revert`. Verified through the product's own read path: a fleet supervisor's PostgREST token returns them.

**It took three attempts, and the two failures are the lesson.** The seeder wrote 0 rows twice and said so
quietly, because the helper swallowed the error that named the cause: `logbook.date` is NOT NULL with no
default, and `status` is a CHECK over `Open/Closed/Resolved` - **"Completed" was my word, not the table's**.
The same vocabulary error the whole wave keeps finding, this time in a seeder rather than a lens.

### What the threads between pages actually look like

`tools/report_journey_threads.py` classifies every readable hop the walks have taken - the page carries the
next one in its OWN body, it is reachable only through the shared drawer, or there is no way onward at all.
A hop is counted only if its page arrived and finished rendering, because a thread read on a page that
bounced says nothing about the page it was supposed to be.

Across the first 61 readable hops:

| | hops | share |
|---|---|---|
| the page's own link | 14 | 23% |
| the nav drawer only | 35 | 57% |
| no way onward | 12 | 20% |

**Four pages never carried their own onward link at all** - logbook (14 hops), asset-hub (12), shift-brain
(8), pm-scheduler (7). Every move from them requires opening the drawer. That is not a defect; each page
works and the drawer is one tap away. It is a design observation with a number on it: **a journey where four
fifths of the hops need shared chrome is a set of tools rather than a path**, and the places where a person
is most likely to want the next surface - the alert they just read, the PM they just planned - are exactly
where the page says nothing about where to go next.

**One caveat, stated because the number would otherwise be read as worse than it is.** Most of these hops
were walked BEFORE the nav-mode repair, while a supervisor's drawer was missing Analytics, the Alert Hub and
Reports - so the two dominant *no way onward* pairs (`pm-scheduler -> analytics`, 5, and
`alert-hub -> asset-hub`, 4) are partly that defect rather than a missing link. The report now says so, and
the pairs are re-measured on walks taken after the repair. **A count taken across a fix is two counts.**

### THE WAVE'S FIRST PRODUCT DEFECT: every supervisor navigated with a worker's menu

The journey walks kept reporting *"1 hop(s) have no way onward at all"* on hops whose pages were fully
rendered and settled - `pm-scheduler -> alert-hub`, `pm-scheduler -> analytics`. Unlike the thin readings,
that finding **survived every correction to the reader**, which is what made it worth chasing.

The nav hub was identical on all four pages checked (31 KB, 17 links) and contained **neither
`alert-hub.html` nor `analytics.html`** - while `nav-hub.js` plainly declares both, tagged
`roles: ['supervisor']`. The person walking was a supervisor.

**The mechanism.** `getMode()` reads `wh_nav_mode`; if it holds a valid mode it wins. Otherwise `_defaultMode()`
derives one from `wh_hive_role` **and persists it**. The first page anybody meets renders the hub while nobody
is signed in - so the derivation ran with no role, returned `field`, stored it, and the stored value won for
ever after. Measured live, both by the ordinary arrival and by a control that signed in first:

| | role | stored mode | hub links | Analytics | Alert Hub | Reports |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | supervisor | **field** | 17 | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
| after | supervisor | supervisor | **24** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**Why no per-page test could see it.** Every one of those pages works when you arrive by URL. The defect is
not on a page; it is in the thread between pages. This is precisely the class the full-journey wave was built
for, and it was invisible to 2,437 rows of per-page work.

**The repair keeps the original intent** - *"existing users with an explicit choice keep it"* - by recording
WHY a mode was stored (`wh_nav_mode_src`: `chosen` | `derived` | `guess`). A chosen mode is never touched; a
mode guessed before the role was known is re-derived when the role arrives. Locked by
`tools/prove_nav_mode.mjs` (gate `nav-mode`) with teeth in both directions, because a repair that hands
everyone the supervisor menu is a worse defect than the one it fixes: a worker still gets the tight field
set, and a supervisor who chose Field keeps Field.

**The class worth carrying:** a value derived from identity, cached before identity is known, and never
re-derived. Whenever a default is computed from who somebody is, ask when it is first computed - and if that
can happen before they are known, record whether it was a guess or a decision.

### W3-LN's Internal-Control lens, and a warning the critic sweep needs before it runs

A learn article is the front door for a stranger with no account and no reason to trust it, so it owes
sources and a freshness statement. Measured across all 54: **54 name sources or the authority behind them
(DOE, IEA, DOLE, PSA, ERC, PSME…) and 54 say how fresh they are.** Gate `learn-provenance`.

**Only 2 of 54 carry a `.wh-source-chip`, and that is deliberately NOT a finding.** No generator emits one
for learn pages; the two that have it picked it up during other work on those specific articles. The chip is
a product-surface convention, and prose that says *"According to the Department of Energy"* with a dateline
serves the same reader need on a page that is mostly prose.

**This matters for the wave that comes next.** The critic program is scheduled to grade all 53 learn articles
on the full rubric, and the rubric's `E3` dimension looks for exactly that chip. Run as-is, it will return
**51 failures for a chip those pages were never designed to have** - a rubric-fit problem wearing the costume
of 51 defects, and the largest single block of false findings this wave could still produce. **Fixed in the rubric, before the sweep ran.** `E3` now asks whether a READER can check the claim, and on
an article accepts the sentence: a page under `/learn/` that names its sources or the authority behind
them AND states its freshness scores the dimension in full, while every product surface still owes the
chip. `rubric-parity` stays green (102 prose / 102 spec). The 51 findings were prevented rather than
triaged - which is the cheaper half of the same lesson, and the only half available before a sweep runs.

Recording it before the sweep runs is the cheap half of the lesson this whole wave keeps re-learning:
**a checker meeting a page type it was not written for produces confident nonsense at scale.**

### W3-CL's Internal-Control lens: all 60 calculators cite their standard, and the seventh vocabulary catch

An engineering calculator's number goes into a drawing, so it owes a citation an engineer can actually look
up. Measured from the generated pages: **60 of 60 cite a standard with the number they would open it at** -
`ASHRAE 62.1:2022 Ventilation Rate Procedure`, `ISO 22400-2`, `IEEE 18-2012`, `PEC 2017 Art. 4.50`,
`Philippine Plumbing Code §P-1101`, `CTI STD-201`. Standing gate `calc-citations`.

**That number moved twice before it settled, and the route is worth keeping.** It read 60, then 11, then 60:

| pass | verdict | what was actually being measured |
|---|---|---|
| first | 60/60 name standard AND clause | the clause half matched **HTML tag names** - `<section a…`, `<article c…`, the words *"table t"* - because the pattern allowed a letter after the keyword. Right answer, wrong reason. |
| second | 11/60 name a clause | tightened to demand a digit, which was correct - and then demanded the literal words *Table* or *Section*, which is **my** convention, not an engineer's |
| third | 60/60 cite specifically | the real question: does the citation carry the number you open the book at? `ISO 22400-2` and `ASHRAE 62.1:2022` do; a bare "ASHRAE" would not |

**A live read is what exposed the first pass.** The browser, reading rendered text, found no clause where the
static check found sixty - and a tag is invisible to one instrument and a citation to the other. **When two
instruments disagree, the disagreement is the finding**; here it cost an hour and produced a checker that
knows the difference between markup and a reference.

And the second pass is the more familiar failure: correcting an error by over-correcting into my own
vocabulary, which is the same move this wave has caught seven other times wearing seven other costumes.

Getting there took one more correction of the kind this wave keeps making. A first pass demanded an acronym
followed immediately by a digit and reported that **17 calculators named no standard at all** - the septic
tank, the grease trap, the storm drain, water treatment, the boilers. Reading four of them refuted it in one
line each:

| calculator | what it actually cites | why the pattern missed it |
|---|---|---|
| septic tank | **Plumbing Code §P-1101** | Philippine plumbing code, not an NFPA-style acronym |
| storm drain | **DPWH Blue Book**, Rational Method | a national agency and a method, not a numbered standard |
| water treatment | **PNS 1998 / PNSDW** | Philippine National Standards |
| boiler steam | **ASME BPVC Section I** | BPVC is letters; the pattern demanded a digit |

**The pages the checker accused were the ones most correctly localized.** A checker that only knows
NFPA/ASHRAE/ISO shapes will always flag a Philippine platform's plumbing and sanitary work first - which is
the whole vocabulary lesson, arriving through the front door of a wave built to avoid it. The gate now knows
the National Plumbing Code, the PSME Code, PNS, PNSDW, DPWH, DENR DAO, PD/RA numbers, BPVC, and the named
methods (Rational, Hazen-Williams, Darcy, Manning, Colebrook).

### W3-SC's Internal-Control lens, answered from the sources - and deliberately not called a finding

The shared-component wave asks whether a shared piece ever keeps one person's state where the next person
inherits it. That is answerable from the sources before any browser opens: of 13 storage writes across the
shared scripts, **3 carry an owner in the key and 10 do not.**

Most of the ten are device-scoped by design and no leak at all - a session id, a signup source, a retry
counter, a told-you-once flag, the analytics consent (which belongs to the browser, not the person). Three
are different in kind: `wh_voice_lang_pref`, `wh_voice_brevity` and `wh_voice_journal_persona` are personal
choices, and the sign-out path clears only `wh_last_worker`. On a shared plant tablet - a cell this wave
walks on purpose - the next person inherits the previous one's voice language, brevity and AI persona.

**It is recorded as a candidate, not a finding, and the counter-argument is why.** The platform already
treats `wh_lang`, the interface language, as a device preference, and nobody would call that a leak; voice
language is the same shape. The one that is genuinely personal is the AI persona. A static read cannot settle
whether these should follow the device or the person - that is a product judgement, and the walk plus Ian's
call decide it.

Saying so costs nothing and protects the wave's credibility: **a night that caught a dozen of its own false
findings should not spend that credit on a design question dressed as a defect.**

### W3-FN opened, and the probe that timed out before the platform did

The function wave asks three things of each of the 62 edge functions: it must refuse a caller holding a real
token for another hive (with a sentinel from that hive absent from the reply), degrade legibly when its
dependency is down, and answer its documented shape to somebody who actually calls it.

Its first run reported three functions that *"never returned - a hang is not a degradation a person can
read"*. **The platform bounds those calls; my prober did not wait for the bound.** `_shared/ai-chain.ts`
wraps every provider call in `AbortSignal.timeout(60000)` and allows one jittered retry pass before degrading
to `"{}"` - a worst case of about two minutes, by design. The prober gives up at 35 seconds, so *"the call
never returned"* was the probe abandoning it, reported as three functions hanging.

Corrected: a timeout in the prober is **not evidence** when the source shows a bounded provider call with a
degradation path, and remains a finding when nothing in the source bounds it at all. Re-run, `agentic-rag-loop`
passes all three lenses and `ai-eval-runner`'s timeouts are reported as unreadable rather than as hangs - six
false findings prevented in eight functions.

**The rule this adds to the wave's collection: a probe's patience must exceed the platform's own.** A
timeout shorter than the system's declared bound cannot distinguish "it hung" from "I left".

### A page that is WAITING is not a page that failed

`analytics-report.html` was read still-thin in **4 of 4** walks that touched it - the highest rate of any
page - and each time the walk recorded *"never finished rendering, wait ran out"*. Reading the page settles
it: the report is built only when somebody presses **Generate**. Its resting state is a small, action-first
shell around that button, and 527 characters is the design rather than a failure.

That is the third distinct way this wave's render floor has been wrong, and the pattern in all three is the
same: **a size threshold is a proxy, and every proxy eventually meets a case it was not written for.** First
it called load-thinned pages "leads nowhere"; then it called a two-phase load "almost nothing"; now it called
a deliberately compact page "never finished".

The rule is no longer size alone. A step is thin only if it is **short AND offers nothing to do** - three or
more of the page's own visible controls means the page is complete and waiting for a person, not broken. The
settle loop uses the same test, so the walk stops spending its whole budget on a page that finished in a
second.

### What the journey wave costs to walk, measured rather than hoped

At the throughput this host actually delivers - about two and a half minutes per whole story, once the
session is cached, the chains are read up front and only one walk runs at a time:

| tier | journeys | browser time |
|---|---|---|
| A base cast | 130 | ~5.4 h |
| B device + Filipino | 381 | ~15.9 h |
| C overlays | 197 | ~8.2 h |
| D lifetimes | 16 | ~0.7 h |
| **all four** | **724** | **~30 h** |

That is the honest size of W3-JN, and it is why the runner is built the way it is: one archetype at a time,
a lock that refuses a second drive, a wait for the stack before each archetype, a re-walk of any run that
lost it, and banking after each archetype rather than at the end. **A thirty-hour walk that has to restart
from zero after a wedge is not a walk; a thirty-hour walk that banks every six journeys is a queue.**

The order is deliberate: tier A first, because it is the only tier where every archetype-and-vertical pair
appears exactly once - it is the map. B, C and D are the same stories under a different device, language,
moment or condition, and they are worth most once the base cast is known to hold.

### The re-walk confirms the fix, in the only way that counts

`J1` was re-walked after the nav-mode repair, and the measurement it was queued for came back clean: **zero
hops with no way onward, in every hive.** Before the repair, `J1` and `J2` reported dead hops on
`pm-scheduler -> alert-hub` and `pm-scheduler -> analytics` - the two surfaces the supervisor's drawer was
missing. After it, `W33` (Baguio Textile Mills) and `W34` (Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet) walk all six steps,
keep the identity and read their chain, and pass.

That is the loop closing on itself: a journey walk found a defect no per-page test could see, the repair was
verified in three directions and locked behind a gate, and **the same walk re-run is now the evidence that
the fix worked** - not an argument that it should have.

The rows that still hold in that batch hold for reasons of the moment rather than of the product: two casts
met `WH_DB_TIMEOUT` from a local auth server under load, and one story arrived at 1 of 6 pages while a
62-function contract sweep had the host. Both are the contention this wave has now made structurally
impossible - every browser prover takes a single shared slot before it launches, so the suite's concurrent
gates queue instead of racing. **The findings from before that lock are about the lock's absence.**

### A fix invalidates the evidence taken before it

The nav-mode repair changed what a supervisor's drawer contains, so every hop the walks measured toward
Analytics, the Alert Hub or Reports **before** that repair is stale: those hops read `none` for a reason that
no longer exists. `J1` and `J2` are queued for a re-walk on that basis alone - `W35` (Ramos Jeepney Line) was
held for exactly one finding, *"1 hop has no way onward at all"* on `pm-scheduler -> alert-hub`, and that hop
is precisely what the fix restored.

This is a small discipline with a sharp edge: **a repair does not only change the product, it expires a
subset of the measurements taken against it.** The queue now carries the re-walk explicitly rather than
leaving those rows held against a defect that is gone, and `tools/report_journey_threads.py` prints the same
caveat above its census so the number is never read as current when half its hops predate the fix.

### RETRACTED: content waits behind identity

The section below was recorded as *"a correlation across six pages plus a mechanism, not a proven cause"* and
marked for re-check on wider data. **The wider data refutes it.** Measured across every walk so far - 12
pages with three or more readable reads each, counting how often each was read still under the render floor
against how many sequential identity round-trips it makes:

| page | read thin | reads | identity hops |
|---|---|---|---|
| analytics-report | 100% | 4 | 4 |
| pm-scheduler | 67% | 18 | 6 |
| inventory | 50% | 6 | 4 |
| asset-hub | 35% | 20 | 6 |
| alert-hub | 21% | 14 | 5 |
| **logbook** | **0%** | **24** | **9** |
| analytics | 0% | 15 | 2 |

The median identity-hop count is **4 for the pages that read thin at least half the time and 4 for the pages
that never do** - and `logbook`, with the most identity hops of any page measured, never read thin once in
24 reads. The mechanism was plausible, the six-page table was convincing, and the relationship is not there.

**What survives:** some pages consistently need longer than the walk's budget on this host, and which pages
those are is stable. Why is still open, and the honest place to answer it is a quiet host, not a wider regex.

**What this cost, and why it was cheap:** the claim was hedged when it was written, so retracting it is a
paragraph rather than a retraction of banked evidence. **A finding recorded with its confidence attached can
be withdrawn; one recorded as fact has to be defended.**

### The journeys' first substantive finding: content waits behind identity

Across every J1 and J2 walk, the same pages were repeatedly caught still empty and the same pages were always
full - and the readings were identical to the character, which is the signature of a reader arriving before
the page fills rather than a page that is broken. The question worth asking is *why those pages*.

Counting the identity round-trips each page makes before its first data call answers it:

| page | `auth.getSession` | `restoreIdentityFromSession` | `validateHiveMembership` | how the walks read it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| analytics | 1 | 1 | 0 | always full (5,120 chars) |
| alert-hub | 2 | 3 | 0 | usually full (4,995) |
| shift-brain | 1 | 2 | 2 | mixed (914 - 3,928) |
| logbook | 3 | 2 | 4 | usually thin (916 - 1,196) |
| asset-hub | 2 | 2 | 2 | usually thin (609) |
| **pm-scheduler** | **3** | **1** | **2** | **never filled inside a journey** |

`pm-scheduler`'s `init()` is the clearest case: it awaits `restoreIdentityFromSession`, then
`auth.getSession`, then `validateHiveMembership` - three sequential round-trips - before anything asks for a
PM. When the local auth service is slow (and on this host it is: the walks also collect `WH_DB_TIMEOUT` on
sign-in), the page holds at its shell with nothing to read.

**This is an Adaptability finding, not a bug.** Each await is individually correct - the page must know who
is asking before it shows a hive's work. What a person meets is the compound: the more identity hops a page
makes in sequence, the longer it shows them an empty screen with no explanation, and the ordering is the same
whether the walk is fast or slow. The candidate improvements are to overlap the data read with the identity
check where the read is already hive-scoped and RLS-protected anyway, or to say *"checking your access"*
rather than showing an empty page.

**Stated honestly: this is a correlation across six pages plus a mechanism, not a proven cause.** It is
recorded as the journey wave's first substantive candidate and is re-checked on a quiet host, where a page
that still will not fill is the page's problem and one that fills is the host's.

### W3-AR pre-sorted, and the sixth narrow search

The 79 empty (page, layer) squares were sorted before walking by asking each page's source whether it shows
any evidence of the layer it owes. Reading the page ALONE said **fifteen** layers were absent outright - ten
of them rate limiting, on achievements, analytics-report, audit-log, founder-console, integrations,
marketplace-admin, pm-scheduler, project-manager, project-report and skillmatrix.

All ten load `utils.js`, which carries twenty-two rate-limit references and the central `whAiErrorMapper`.
Counting each page **plus the scripts it loads** - which is what a page IS to the person using it - the
absent count falls to **zero**: all 79 squares have something to grade, and the walk decides what a person
actually sees.

That is the sixth time in one session that a search scoped to where I expected the answer produced an
accusation the platform did not deserve: the nav drawer, the alert table, the settle gap, the function
callers, the article call-to-action, and now the shared error handler. **Shared chrome is part of the page**
- the rule was already written down after a page-floor walk counted the hub's buttons as the page's own, and
it needed applying to a static scan too.

### W3-LN's first finding, and the false one it nearly was

The learn wave's Functionality lens asks whether the tool an article sends you to opens and does the job the
article promised. Asked statically across all 54 articles, the first answer looked damning: **only 6 of 54
link to any of the platform's 60 free calculators**, while all 54 funnel to a sign-up. That is a real
measurement and it was about to become a finding for 48 rows.

Matching each calculator-less article to its nearest calculator is what refuted it. Of 48 articles, **one**
produced a confident match, and that match was wrong (an FMEA bottling-line worked example paired with a wire
sizing calculator). The overlap is absent because the articles are practice guides - FMEA, lock-out/tag-out,
shift handover, CMMS-versus-spreadsheet - and the calculators are engineering sizing tools. *"An article
should link to a calculator"* was my expected shape, not the platform's; the articles name the surfaces they
are actually about, and they link to those (analytics 9, logbook 7, asset-hub 5, pm-scheduler 5).

**What survived is small, exact and worth fixing: three articles offered a reader nothing to DO but sign up**
- `best-free-cmms-software-philippines`, `workhive-vs-maintainx-comparison`, and
`workhive-vs-upkeep-free-cmms-comparison`. All three are the comparison articles somebody reads *while
deciding*, which is exactly where a thing to try is worth more than a form. Each now closes by naming two
free calculators that need no account, beside the sign-up rather than instead of it. Re-measured: **zero**
articles offer nothing but the sign-up.

The pattern is the night's pattern, one more time: **a measurement that indicts 48 surfaces is a hypothesis
about my vocabulary; the one that indicts three is a finding.**

### The reading that was stable, reproducible and wrong

`pm-scheduler.html` read **493 characters** on every hive, on every run, loaded and quiet alike. That
stability is what made it convincing: the walk's render floor had been calling thin steps "unreadable, blame
the host", and a number that repeats exactly is not a host. So the floor was split - a step still showing
skeletons is unreadable, a step that settled clean and is still thin is a **finding about what the person was
shown** - and this one was about to be written up as a defect.

Opened alone, with a longer wait, the same page renders **2,617 characters** of real content. It paints its
shell in under a second, holds still while its PM list is in flight, and only then fills. The settle loop was
waiting for the text to stop changing, and the text had stopped changing - in the gap between the shell and
the answer.

**Two rules came out of it, and both are now in the instrument.** A page is not settled while it is still
asking: the walk requires no REST or RPC read in flight, and none for 1.2 seconds, before it believes a
reading. And **reproducibility proves the reader is consistent, never that the reading is true** - "the same
493 in every hive on every run" is exactly what a systematically early reader produces.

The same pass found the identity oracle passing any step whose hive key was EMPTY (`!hive || hive ===
expected`) - which is precisely the state a page leaves behind when it revokes a member and drops to solo
scope. The one page that can throw a member out would have read as *identity kept*. It compares against the
expected value now, never against "or nothing".

**And the sign-ins were the throughput problem.** Every story re-authenticated, so a wave of 724 journeys
meant 724 sign-ins against a local auth server that answers `WH_DB_TIMEOUT` when this host is busy - walks
failing because the probe asked the same question 724 times, not because the platform refused. The session is
minted once per person-and-hive and replayed as storage state, which is also what a real person carries from
one page to the next. With that and the settle loop, a whole story costs about two minutes instead of seven.

### The host is part of the instrument

This box has ~0.3 GB free of 7.8 GB with the Supabase stack running. Two node jobs at once produced a docker
engine returning 500, a `docker exec` that never came back, and a six-journey walk **frozen at zero CPU with
no output and no error** - because `execSync` waits for ever by default. Every shell-out in the wave-3
provers now carries a timeout and a kill signal, and the walks run one at a time. The stack recovered on its
own the moment the browser load stopped, so nothing was restarted: the evidence said "starved", not "broken".

## §LX · The LAYER-UX wave — what a person FEELS when a layer misbehaves (Ian, 2026-09-06)

Ian: *"we have to expand the trajectories more to those uncharted, uncovered, unexplored... I want it more to improve
the UFAI UI UX for every Full Stack SaaS Layer I have"*, and *"those layers that have less trajectories, we have to
make more for those."* He chose the framing (**what the person feels**, not whether the layer is internally correct)
and the size (**exhaustive across all 13 layers**).

**THE AXIS DID NOT EXIST UNTIL THIS WAVE.** Rows have carried a `layers` field since the P-program, but only the
seeder ever wrote it: on 2026-09-06 it was populated on **704 rows and empty on 725** — every T, VP, VD and VM row,
which is to say every persona journey, the half of the program most about what a person experiences. A per-layer
number over half the rows is not a number. `tools/backfill_trajectory_layers.py` closed that: every row now names
the layers its journey crosses, multi-tagged the way the field already worked (597 rows carried more than one
before the backfill). 95 of the 725 matched no rule and took the stated default `["F"]`; the script prints that
count on every run so the default can never quietly become the answer.

**WHY HOSTING IS THE POINT.** The same day, a walk found the repo shipping Cloudflare `_headers` and a
`netlify.toml` to a **Vercel** host, which reads neither — so no security header had ever been served in production
and `/_fixtures/` answered 200. There were 1,429 trajectories and not one asked what the deployed origin actually
hands a person. Hosting held 38 rows after backfill and was the least-WALKED layer of all, 18 of 38.

**THE DEFICIT, AND THE HEADLINE MOVING.** With every row tagged, the generated header could state the gap against a
90-row target: CI 15 (+75) · L 31 (+59) · LB 33 (+57) · H 38 (+52) · RL 45 (+45) · S 66 (+24). `tools/seed_layer_ux_wave.py`
seeded those **316 rows** at `specced`, and the headline dropped from **91.4% of 1,377 to 74.3% of 1,693** the moment
they landed. That drop is the honest direction and the generator computes it — the same discipline as the tightening
earlier the same day, which moved the number 64.6% → 49.9% when "closed" began requiring the right instrument.

| Layer | Lens — each row is this sentence on one surface |
|---|---|
| **CI** CI/CD | a release lands mid-session and the page changes under you · a feature arrives half-on · a migration ships ahead of its screen · you cannot say which version broke · a rollback takes your unsaved work |
| **L** Logs | the error you hit leaves no trace · "something went wrong" where the log knew exactly what · nothing to quote to support · your failure reached nobody |
| **LB** Scaling | past twenty people the page slows and never says so · the list stops paginating · the export carries less than the screen · two of you act at once and one loses silently |
| **H** Hosting | a feature dead in prod because the origin sends no header · a link that 404s in prod and opens for its author · a redirect that loses what you arrived with · an asset re-downloaded every visit |
| **RL** Rate limits | refused without being told when to return · someone else spent your hive's limit · your retry makes it worse and nothing warns you |
| **S** Security | refused in a way that tells you nothing, or too much · you can see it but must not act, and the page does not say which |

**THE WALK ORDER AND ITS INSTRUMENTS** follow §LW.1 — the lens picks the instrument, and a layer with no MCP is a
queue item, not an excuse. Thinnest first: **CI** (github MCP + the gate suite), **L** (sentry + grafana, the outside
witnesses), **H** (raw-http against the deployed origin — `tools/prove_prod_headers.mjs` already exists — plus a
**Vercel MCP to connect**), **LB** (postgres MCP for query cost as a hive grows, playwright for what the page does,
**k6 to install** for the local load tier), **RL** (a raw-http burst plus postgres for the bucket), **S** (the
`tenant-refusal` gate built this wave). Two MCPs to connect proactively — **Vercel**, and bringing **chrome-devtools**
live for the caching lenses — and one tool to install, **k6**.

## §LW · The LIVE-WALK wave and its MCP instruments (Ian, 2026-09-06)

Ian: *"live deepwalk each trajectory or group of categories, but do not repeat what you already done"*, then
*"utilize appropriate and applicable MCP that we have or do not have, connect it, according to the trajectories"*,
and for the header: **two buckets on live evidence**.

**Why the wave exists.** The registry said 99% GATED while only 537 of 1,377 in-scope rows had ever been exercised
against the running system. Reading each row's own `basis` for the KIND of evidence it holds separates a walk from a
claim: `live` (an instrument RAN), `board` (a page's score inherited), `gate` (a static gate), `prose` (an argument).
`tools/live_walk_manifest.py` is that classifier, the header's source, the gate `live-walk-manifest`, and the
**no-repeat ledger** — a row classified `live` is never walked again.

### §LW.1 The MCP doctrine (Ian, 2026-09-06)

> *"We have to maximize the usage of our MCPs, we have to use appropriately the MCPs depending on the type or kind of
> trajectories... but if there are needed other MCPs we don't have, we have to proactively connect another kind of MCP."*

Four rules, in force for every walk from here:

1. **The instrument is chosen by the KIND of trajectory, never by habit.** A journey is walked step by step; a contract
   is asked over HTTP; a number is checked against the database; a crash is read from the error tracker. Using one
   instrument for every kind is how a program ends up 99% gated and 39% walked.
2. **Prefer the OUTSIDE witness.** Where a claim can be checked from another system - Postgres for state, Sentry for
   crashes, Grafana for liveness, the mail connector for delivery - use it, because a page cannot be cross-examined
   with its own story. The strongest evidence in this wave came from exactly that: the DB said 4 pending while the
   tile said 4, and the audit table showed what the click actually wrote.
3. **A kind with no matching MCP is a QUEUE ITEM, not an excuse.** When a family has no suitable server, connecting one
   is the first slice of that family's walk. This is the same rule as "build the structure": we do not downgrade the
   lens to fit the tools we happen to have.
4. **Batch with the library, walk with the MCP.** A 40-surface sweep is one command through the Playwright library and
   400 tool calls through the MCP; a persona journey is the reverse, because each step's snapshot decides the next.
   Both drive the same Chromium - the choice is the shape of the walk, and it is written into the table below.

**Connected today:** playwright · postgres (local 54322) · sentry (self-hosted :8000) · github · crawl4ai ·
chrome-devtools (added in this wave) · the claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Drive, Supabase-cloud).
**Configured but down:** grafana — *2026-09-09: `workhive_grafana` was observed **Up 3 hours** in a full
container listing this session, so "stopped for RAM" is at least sometimes stale. Recorded as an observation
with its time rather than a new standing claim: a later listing, taken while a browser walk had the host, could
not answer at all. Re-read the container list before relying on either state.*
**Came up 2026-09-09:** obsidian (previously "port open, handshake failing" — it now hands off cleanly and its
vault tools are available, so the knowledge-manager family has its outside witness).
**Configured, NOT authorised here:** the claude.ai **Google Calendar** and **Slack** connectors need their OAuth
flow run from claude.ai connector settings; a non-interactive session cannot do it, so any row that needs a
calendar or a Slack delivery is blocked on that consent, not on a missing server.

**Proactively queued, each tied to the rows it unblocks** (rule 3):

| Missing capability | Why no current server answers it | Rows waiting | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| accessibility engine (axe) | the a11y family needs violations ON DEMAND during a walk, not a batch file written hours earlier | a11y deep, 33 | connect an axe MCP; until then the platform's own axe runner + the playwright MCP tab walk |
| HTTP headers / redirects | `crawl4ai` returns markdown and cannot see headers; the npm fetch server does not exist and `uv` is absent here | `_headers is prod-only` 13, plus canonical/robots in the funnels | build a small local MCP or keep curl, decided when the funnels family runs |
| mail delivery witness | a report journey ends in an inbox, and nothing in the repo can see one | report-sender + notification arcs | use the claude.ai **Gmail** connector as the delivery witness |
| local Supabase admin | the claude.ai Supabase connector points at the CLOUD project, not our stack | edge/API + grounding walks | keep invoke + psql, or point a self-hosted Supabase MCP at 127.0.0.1:54321 |

### §LW.2 · WALK THE TRAJECTORIES THROUGH THE MCPs — the default, so triage happens in REAL TIME (Ian, 2026-09-09)

> *"I prefer you drive the roadmap realtime so that you can triage realtime, so that we can move fast on
> completing the headline percentage to 100%"*, and then: *"I want you to put it in our roadmap that we have to
> do the trajectories using MCPs, so that we can proceed realtime."*

This **supersedes the free choice in rule 4 above**. Rule 4 said batch with the library, walk with the MCP, and
left the shape to judgement. The default is now the MCP: a trajectory is driven step by step through the
playwright and postgres servers, with the findings read AS THEY LAND. A headless batch script is the exception,
taken only when a sweep is genuinely uniform and nothing in it needs deciding mid-flight.

**Why, measured on 2026-09-09 rather than argued.** The Tier-A journey wave was run the old way — one
`prove_full_journeys.mjs --tier A` process, 130 stories, headless. What that cost:

- **~3 hours before a single finding could be acted on.** Everything the walk learned sat inside the process
  until it wrote its JSON at the end. Two seed gaps it had already proven — a fleet hive whose parts have never
  moved, four hives with nobody to send a report to — would have waited hours to be seen.
- **It took the machine down once.** 130 stories in one process reached 158MB free of 7.8GB with 33 chromium
  processes alive, and the Docker engine beside it began answering 500. The run had to be killed at story 20.
- **It manufactured findings.** Its own load pushed a sub-millisecond query past `community.html`'s 15s client
  bound, so the page honestly reported a connection problem that existed only because the walk was standing on
  the machine — and the walk recorded it as a defect. Loading that page by hand through the MCP, as the same
  person, showed a correct empty state. A batch cannot notice that about itself; an operator watching can.
- **What real-time triage found in the same window:** the missing `skill_profiles` across all three fleet hives,
  fixed generator-first mid-run, flipping journeys to passing on the next pass rather than the next session.

**The rules that follow:**

1. **Drive with the MCP by default.** playwright for the walk, postgres for the effect, the mail connector for a
   delivery — one step, one reading, decided before the next step. This is what makes a finding actionable at
   the moment it appears rather than at the end of a run.
2. **Triage as it lands, and fix what is fixable immediately.** A seed gap found at story 30 is filled before
   story 60 walks, so the rest of the wave measures the platform as repaired. Waiting banks the same failure
   dozens of times.
3. **Keep the batch prover as the RATCHET, not the discovery tool.** `prove_full_journeys.mjs` and its siblings
   stay, registered as gates, to re-prove in bulk what an MCP walk has already established — that is what a gate
   is for. Discovery moves to the MCP.
4. **Serial, always, on this host.** Whatever the shape, one browser at a time: every false finding this session
   produced was contention, and the DB answered a plain read in 180s while a walk had the machine.
5. **A kind with no MCP is still a queue item** (rule 3 above is unchanged) — the answer to a missing server is
   to connect one, never to fall back to a batch script and call the lens covered.

### The instruments, per family

| Family | Instrument | MCP / runtime | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| degradation & state | `tools/prove_db_pages_degradation.mjs` (both modes, 34 surfaces) | playwright library | `db-pages-degradation` |
| render & CSS | `tools/prove_render_contract.mjs` (4 lenses, 41 surfaces) | playwright library | `render-contract` |
| edge & API contracts | `tools/prove_edge_contract.mjs` (4 asks, 62 functions) | local edge stack over HTTP | `edge-contract` |
| data honesty | `tools/prove_data_honesty.mjs` (basis, windows, caps) | playwright library | `data-honesty` |
| **journeys + the 222 cross-cutting arcs** | **step-by-step walk** | **playwright MCP** (snapshot → act → snapshot) + **postgres MCP** (the state actually changed) | per-arc |
| **ops & observability** | health/cron liveness read from the outside | **grafana MCP** (container `workhive_grafana`, start it for the family) + **sentry MCP** | per-arc |
| mobile deep | `tools/prove_phone_fit.mjs` extended (768 landscape, install) | playwright library + **chrome-devtools MCP** | `phone-fit`, `phone-fit-360` |
| a11y deep | keyboard path / landmarks / announcements | **playwright MCP** (a real tab walk) | to build |
| public funnels | arrival as a crawler sees it | **crawl4ai MCP** + curl for headers | to build |

**Library vs MCP, decided once:** a 40-surface sweep is ONE command through the Playwright library and 400 tool calls
through the MCP, so batch lenses use the library. The MCP is the right instrument where the walk is a JOURNEY — a
persona doing a task step by step, where each step's snapshot decides the next — and where the evidence lives in
another system (Grafana, Sentry, Postgres). Both drive the same Chromium; the choice is about the shape of the walk.

## ★THE TARGET — all 500 trajectories at 100% each

**Ian, 2026-08-31: _"we have to finished all 200 trajectories to each 100%, put it to our roadmap"_ —
and later the same day, the exhaustive expansion: the program is now T1–T500, and the target spans all
of it.** `.momentum_drive` stays armed for this program.

That is the standing objective, written here rather than left in a session transcript so every future
session reads it before anything else.

**What 100% MEANS, stated so it cannot be reached by flattery.** The registry's pct is fixed per status
(`specced 5 · walked 25 · fixed 60 · locked 100`), so **100% is `locked`, and nothing else** — and
`tools/validate_trajectory_registry.py` holds `locked` to naming **at least one gate that is registered
in `run_platform_checks.py`**. A trajectory therefore cannot reach 100% by editing a number: it needs a
gate that actually runs on the board. "All 500 at 100%" is exactly **"all 500 locked, each with a
registered, running gate."**

**Where the program stands is ALWAYS the generated scoreboard above — never a count typed here** (a
hand-typed table drifted against the header within a week of being written; the generated block cannot).
Structurally the distance decomposes as:

- **locked** — done; nothing to re-earn while its gates stay green on the board.
- **locking** — gate built; finish the row's own `Remaining:` line, then lock. The cheapest closures.
- **fixing** — the genuine build queue of the original 200.
- **walked** — capstones sequenced last by design (T196, T200).
- **specced** — the T201–T500 expansion catalog: honest 5% until each is actually walked.

**The pct-weighted headline must not be read as progress toward this target.** The doctrine's own rule
applies to this very number: one metric at a comfortable value while the axis Ian named — *every*
trajectory at 100% — is measured only by the locked count. Adding the 300 expansion arcs correctly
DROPPED the headline; a header that cannot drop cannot be honest.

**The honest sequencing, from the 62 `locking` rows' own `Remaining:` lines:**
- **1** (`T179`) is waiting on the wave-close **re-earn only** — it closes when the restamp lands.
- **57** carry real, named remaining work — the cheapest distance to 100%, because each already has its
  gate built and sits at 72–99%.
- **4** carry no `Remaining:` line and need their state re-read before they can be claimed either way.

`WAVE_CLOSE_QUEUE.md` (generated) holds every one of those remainder lines; it is the work list for this
target, not a summary of it.

### Wave W — Security & adversarial personas (T361–T384, 24)
- **T361** · BOLA: guess another hive's asset id — _adversary enumerates /rest/v1/assets?id=<other-hive> hoping the ref, not RLS, is the only guard_
- **T362** · Broken function-level auth: worker hits admin RPC — _signed-in worker calls an owner-only RPC directly, betting the button was the only gate_
- **T363** · JWT-in-body trust — _attacker sends a claim in the request body hoping an edge function trusts it over the verified JWT_
- **T364** · Tenant boundary via forged hive_id — _attacker posts a write with someone else's hive_id to cross the tenant wall_
- **T365** · Mass assignment on profile update — _attacker adds role:owner to a profile PATCH hoping the column is unguarded_
- **T366** · IDOR on marketplace order — _buyer edits an order id in the URL to read a stranger's transaction and address_
- **T367** · Stored XSS in a logbook entry — _attacker plants <script> in free text hoping a consumer renders it unescaped_
- **T368** · SQL/PostgREST injection via filter param — _attacker crafts a filter operator to widen a query past its intended row set_
- **T369** · SSRF via a webhook/callback URL — _attacker points an outbound integration URL at an internal address_
- **T370** · Rate-limit / brute force on login — _attacker scripts the login edge function to credential-stuff_
- **T371** · Password-reset token reuse — _attacker replays a supervisor-reset-password token after it should have burned_
- **T372** · Enumerate users via signup error deltas — _attacker distinguishes 'exists' from 'created' by response timing/text_
- **T373** · Invite-code forgery / replay — _attacker crafts or reuses a hive invite code to self-join_
- **T374** · Privilege escalation via stale membership — _removed member's cached session still writes before the wall catches up_
- **T375** · File-upload content smuggling — _attacker uploads a mislabeled file to a storage bucket to bypass a MIME gate_
- **T376** · Signed-URL scope abuse — _attacker widens or reuses a storage signed URL past its object_
- **T377** · CSRF on a state-changing GET — _attacker tricks a session into a cross-site state change on a non-idempotent endpoint_
- **T378** · Webhook signature bypass (gcash-receipt-inbound) — _attacker posts a forged payment webhook without a valid signature to mark a txn paid_
- **T379** · Race to double-spend a marketplace credit — _attacker fires two concurrent redemptions of the same credit_
- **T380** · Exfil via export-hive-data as a low-role — _low-privilege member triggers a full-hive export they should not receive_
- **T381** · Prompt injection into an AI agent — _attacker plants instructions in user content that an AI orchestrator later executes_
- **T382** · Denial-of-wallet on a metered AI endpoint — _attacker loops an expensive AI call to exhaust the owner's budget_
- **T383** · Open redirect on return-url params — _attacker crafts ?return= to bounce a signed-in user to a phishing origin_
- **T384** · Audit-log tampering / gap — _attacker performs an action on a path that writes no audit row, hiding the trail_

### Wave X — Accessibility spectrum (T385–T402, 18)
- **T385** · Screen-reader: complete a work order end-to-end — _a blind supervisor drives logbook->assign with NVDA/VoiceOver, intent = finish without sight_
- **T386** · Keyboard-only: no mouse anywhere — _a motor-impaired user tabs through every interactive control, focus never trapped or lost_
- **T387** · Low-vision at 400% zoom — _a partially-sighted user zooms to 400%; no content clipped, no horizontal scroll trap_
- **T388** · Color-blind: status conveyed beyond hue — _a deuteranope reads asset health where red/green alone would be ambiguous_
- **T389** · Switch-access single-input navigation — _a quadriplegic user drives the app with one switch and scanning_
- **T390** · Voice-control (Dragon/Voice Access) — _a user speaks 'click Assign' — every control has a spoken-accessible name_
- **T391** · Screen-magnifier follow-focus — _a low-vision user's magnifier follows focus and new content into the viewport_
- **T392** · Deaf/HoH: captions & no audio-only cues — _a Deaf user needs every audio alert mirrored visually (voice-journal playback captioned)_
- **T393** · Cognitive load: plain-language + steps — _a user with a cognitive disability needs a long form chunked and jargon explained_
- **T394** · Reduced-motion respected — _a vestibular-disorder user with prefers-reduced-motion sees no parallax/auto-animation_
- **T395** · Reflow at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10) — _content reflows to a single column at 320px with no loss of function_
- **T396** · Focus-visible on every control — _a keyboard user always sees where focus is; no invisible focus ring_
- **T397** · Form errors announced to AT — _a validation error is programmatically associated and announced, not just colored_
- **T398** · Live-region for async updates — _a screen-reader user hears a toast/status change via an aria-live region_
- **T399** · Touch target >=44px on phone — _a user with a tremor can hit every phone control without mis-tapping a neighbor_
- **T400** · Skip-link & landmark navigation — _a screen-reader user jumps past nav to main via a skip link and landmarks_
- **T401** · High-contrast / forced-colors mode — _a Windows High Contrast user retains all borders, icons and state_
- **T402** · Timeout & session-extend accessible — _a slow user is warned before a session/auto-save timeout and can extend it_

### Wave Y — New human personas (T403–T420, 18)
- **T403** · DOLE labor inspector reviews compliance — _a government inspector audits permit-to-work and shift records for a Philippine plant_
- **T404** · Insurance assessor verifies maintenance history — _an assessor needs tamper-evident asset maintenance history for a claim_
- **T405** · Procurement officer evaluates a marketplace seller — _a corporate buyer vets a seller's trust signals before a bulk order_
- **T406** · Night-shift lone operator — _a solo night-shift tech logs a fault at 3am with no supervisor online_
- **T407** · Regional manager across many hives — _a multi-site manager compares OEE across the hives they oversee_
- **T408** · Brand-new trainee, day one — _a fresh hire with zero context is onboarded into a hive and their first task_
- **T409** · Contractor working across multiple hives — _an external contractor switches between three client hives without data bleed_
- **T410** · External auditor with read-only, time-boxed access — _an ISO auditor gets scoped, expiring read access to evidence_
- **T411** · Finance controller reconciles marketplace payouts — _a controller ties GCash payouts to completed orders for the books_
- **T412** · Plant safety officer runs an incident review — _a safety officer reconstructs an incident from logbook + audit trail_
- **T413** · HR verifies a worker's skill matrix — _HR confirms certifications before assigning a regulated task_
- **T414** · Vendor/OEM support engineer — _an equipment vendor is granted a narrow window to diagnose one asset_
- **T415** · Executive on a quarterly board review — _a non-technical exec reads the platform's headline reliability KPIs_
- **T416** · Union representative checks fair scheduling — _a rep audits shift assignments for equity across workers_
- **T417** · Data-protection officer handles a subject request — _a DPO fulfils a GDPR/PDPA export/erasure request for one worker_
- **T418** · Retiring supervisor hands over a hive — _an outgoing supervisor transfers ownership and knowledge before leaving_
- **T419** · Seasonal surge temp worker — _a temp is added for a shutdown, works two weeks, is cleanly offboarded_
- **T420** · Regulator cross-checks a public tools claim — _a standards body verifies a public calculator matches the cited standard_

### Wave Z — Data pathology deep (T421–T438, 18)
- **T421** · Partial write: order paid, fulfilment row missing — _a half-committed transaction leaves the UI asserting a state the data denies_
- **T422** · Orphaned child after parent delete — _an asset is deleted but its work orders survive, pointing at nothing_
- **T423** · Timezone-crossing shift at midnight — _a shift spanning midnight in Asia/Manila is counted in the wrong day_
- **T424** · Float precision in a cost/hours rollup — _accumulated rounding drifts a financial total the user can check by hand_
- **T425** · Migration half-state as UX — _a user hits a page mid-migration where old and new columns disagree_
- **T426** · Duplicate rows from a double-submit — _a retried POST creates two identical records the list now shows twice_
- **T427** · Null-vs-zero conflation in a metric — _a missing reading is averaged as 0, deflating an availability number_
- **T428** · Stale cache after a write — _a user saves, navigates, and sees the pre-save value from a warm cache_
- **T429** · Unicode/emoji in names breaks a render — _a worker named with non-Latin script or emoji breaks a downstream label_
- **T430** · Very long text overflows every container — _a 10k-character logbook note must not break layout or truncate silently_
- **T431** · Clock skew between client and server — _a client with a wrong clock stamps events out of order_
- **T432** · Soft-deleted row leaks into an aggregate — _a soft-deleted asset still counts in a hive's totals_
- **T433** · Enum drift: a status value no code handles — _a legacy status value renders as a blank chip nobody planned for_
- **T434** · Cross-hive id collision in a shared table — _two hives' sequences collide in a table keyed without the hive_
- **T435** · Large dataset pagination correctness — _a hive with 50k assets pages without dropping or repeating rows_
- **T436** · Currency/precision at scale (centavos) — _GCash amounts in centavos survive rollup without a rounding leak_
- **T437** · Backfill leaves created_at in the future — _an import sets timestamps ahead of now, breaking 'recent' ordering_
- **T438** · Referential repair crosses the tenant boundary — _an automated fix touches a sibling hive's row — the boundary must hold_

### Wave AA — Financial & economic edge (T439–T454, 16)
- **T439** · Refund after a completed marketplace order — _a buyer disputes; the refund path must reverse credit and ledger cleanly_
- **T440** · Chargeback / reversed GCash payment — _a payment reverses post-fulfilment; the platform reconciles both sides_
- **T441** · Currency & tax on a cross-region sale — _a sale spanning tax jurisdictions computes the right line items_
- **T442** · AI credit exhausted mid-transaction — _an owner's AI budget runs out halfway through a multi-step agent run_
- **T443** · Fraud ring: coordinated fake reviews — _multiple colluding accounts inflate a seller's trust signals_
- **T444** · GCash webhook arrives late / out of order — _a delayed payment webhook lands after the timeout; state reconciles_
- **T445** · Double-charge on a retried checkout — _a network retry must not charge the buyer twice_
- **T446** · Payout to a since-deleted seller account — _a payout is owed to a seller who closed their account_
- **T447** · Price change mid-cart — _a listing's price changes between add-to-cart and checkout_
- **T448** · Subscription proration on plan change — _an owner upgrades mid-cycle; the invoice prorates correctly_
- **T449** · Negative-balance / overdraw guard — _a credit spend that would go negative is refused, not silently allowed_
- **T450** · Escrow release dispute — _buyer and seller disagree on delivery; escrow holds until resolved_
- **T451** · Tax-exempt / invoice-only buyer — _a corporate buyer needs an official receipt and tax handling_
- **T452** · Failed payout retry & idempotency — _a failed payout retries without paying twice_
- **T453** · Promo/discount stacking abuse — _a buyer stacks incompatible promos to underpay_
- **T454** · Financial report reconciles to the ledger — _the analytics revenue figure equals the sum of ledger rows, provably_

### Wave AB — Federation & multi-org (T455–T470, 16)
- **T455** · Parent org rolls up child-hive metrics — _a corporate parent aggregates KPIs across subsidiary hives it owns_
- **T456** · Cross-hive contractor with scoped access — _a contractor sees only the assets each client hive shared, nothing else_
- **T457** · Data-sharing agreement between two hives — _two independent hives share a defined slice under an agreement_
- **T458** · Org-level RBAC above hive roles — _an org admin role spans hives without becoming owner of each_
- **T459** · Subsidiary spins off into its own org — _a child hive is cleanly detached into an independent org with its data_
- **T460** · Shared marketplace seller across hives — _one seller identity operates from several hives without leaking between them_
- **T461** · Central template pushed to all child hives — _a parent publishes a PM template every subsidiary inherits_
- **T462** · Cross-org benchmarking, anonymized — _hives compare against an anonymized peer benchmark without exposing rows_
- **T463** · Merge two hives into one — _an acquisition merges two hives' assets and members without collision_
- **T464** · Federated single sign-on across orgs — _a user with an org SSO identity enters the right hives_
- **T465** · Delegated admin: parent acts for a child — _a parent admin performs an action in a child hive, audited as delegated_
- **T466** · Billing consolidated at the org level — _subsidiaries' usage rolls into one org invoice_
- **T467** · Cross-hive asset transfer — _an asset moves from one hive to another with its history intact_
- **T468** · Region-partitioned data residency — _an org keeps PH and non-PH hive data in the right residency_
- **T469** · Org-wide policy overrides a hive setting — _an org security policy forces a setting a hive cannot loosen_
- **T470** · Guest hive with an expiry date — _a temporary partner hive auto-expires and revokes access on the date_

### Wave AC — Platform-evolution & longitudinal (T471–T484, 14)
- **T471** · Deprecation-as-UX: a retired page's callers — _a user follows an old link to a retired page and is guided forward, not 404'd_
- **T472** · Version-skew client after a deploy — _a user on a stale tab hits new APIs; the app detects and reloads gracefully_
- **T473** · Breaking-change migration a live user is in — _a schema change lands while a user has a half-filled form open_
- **T474** · Multi-year asset history renders — _an asset with five years of records loads and charts without choking_
- **T475** · A feature flag flips mid-session — _a flag toggles while a user is mid-flow; the UI stays coherent_
- **T476** · Old cached service worker serves stale app — _a returning PWA user gets the new version, not a months-old cache_
- **T477** · Data written by a retired feature — _rows created by a since-removed feature still render safely_
- **T478** · Long-dormant account returns — _a user absent a year signs in to a changed platform and re-orients_
- **T479** · Renamed field across an API version — _a field renamed between versions maps for old and new clients_
- **T480** · Historical report reproducibility — _a report run today for last quarter matches what it said then_
- **T481** · Bulk re-embed after a model upgrade — _an embedding model change triggers a backfill without downtime_
- **T482** · Sunset an integration with active users — _a CMMS connector is retired while hives still use it; they're migrated_
- **T483** · Config/default change is backward-safe — _a changed default doesn't silently alter existing hives' behavior_
- **T484** · Terms/consent re-acceptance flow — _a policy update requires re-consent without locking users out of their data_

- **T486** · Agentic-RAG observability traces a run — _an engineer follows one agentic-rag run end-to-end on the page_
- **T487** · PH-intelligence surface is grounded — _the ph-intelligence page's claims trace to real sources, not vibes_

### Wave AE — Compound systemic failures (T493–T500, 8)
- **T493** · DB failover mid-write storm — _the primary fails over while many hives are writing; no lost or dup rows_
- **T494** · Edge-function cold-start cascade under load — _a traffic spike cold-starts many functions at once; the queue holds_
- **T495** · Auth outage with cached sessions active — _the auth service is down but signed-in users must degrade safely_
- **T496** · Storage unavailable during an upload wave — _object storage blips while uploads are in flight; they retry, none corrupt_
- **T497** · Realtime + REST disagree during a partition — _a network partition splits realtime from REST; the UI reconciles on heal_
- **T498** · Third-party (GCash) outage mid-checkout — _the payment provider is down during checkouts; orders park, none half-pay_
- **T499** · Cron/scheduled-agents backlog after downtime — _scheduled jobs pile up during an outage and drain without double-firing_
- **T500** · Region-wide degradation, graceful global — _one region degrades; the platform stays coherent for everyone else_

### P-M · Phone fit: wrap, overflow & menus (added 2026-09-06, Ian's direction)

Ian (2026-09-06): *"extend some trajectories for my entire platform, I've seen some text are become wrapped on their
container in inventory, then also in the hive board, when you tap the more, it overflows and extended on left when using
phone, just refine my thoughts and be proactive to hunt and fix other kinds of issues aside from what I raised."*

**The lens, refined.** The two sightings are one class: the page was laid out for a wide screen and a phone squeezes it
until something gives — a control label breaks onto a second line, a long token spills past its card, a right-anchored
menu runs past the left edge. Four measurable shapes, one prover — `tools/prove_phone_fit.mjs` (390×844 touch context,
signed-in supervisor, every page in the P-H pool; `--page` for one, `--width 360` for a narrower phone):

| Lens | What is measured (live boxes, never classes) | The seed sighting |
|---|---|---|
| no horizontal overflow | `scrollWidth` vs viewport; any visible element PARTIALLY outside either edge (fully-parked closed sheets and decorative off-canvas art excluded) | — |
| labels stay on one line | button / tab / pill / badge / KPI label whose text occupies ≥2 LINE BOXES (a `Range`'s client rects — the padded height read "Save" as 2 lines) | inventory's control labels |
| text stays in its card | a text node whose box ends past its parent's box, the parent not a scroller | inventory's wayfinding crumb: `Spare-Parts Inventory: WorkHive` (nowrap) past a 300px nav |
| menus stay in the viewport | every more/kebab/menu trigger tapped; the revealed menu's box inside `[0, vw]` | hive's More menu: right-anchored 210px at the button; header wraps → button sits left → menu off-screen |

**Fixed at the root, first (2026-09-06):** hive's `wireHiveMenu` clamps the menu after opening (measure → re-anchor left
or right so it stays ≥8px inside the viewport); wayfinding strips `: WorkHive` from the crumb (only `·|—-` were stripped)
and the current-page span ellipsizes itself (text-overflow on an inline-flex box never reaches a child span). Both are
shared: every page's crumb, every page that hosts a right-anchored menu inherits the rule.

**Lock plan.** Rows enter `specced` (the honest drop in the header %). A page's four rows move together: the prover's
pass over the page = the walk (findings receipted per row), the fix cluster lands, the page reads `ok` at 390 and 360 →
`locking` on the registered gate **`phone-fit`** (`run_platform_checks`), `locked` by the full board (Ian's gate).

in both. `tools/validate_family_rubric_ratchet.py` (F7) existed and passed but was **registered nowhere** — now on
the board; P1/P2 and 63 green-lens rows lock on it. The board's `PAGES` grew 32 → 42 (the ten unwalked root pages),
and a new gate, `board-covers-roster` (`tools/validate_board_covers_roster.py`), now fails whenever the page roster
carries a root page the board does not grade — a page may be excused only by name, with a reason. A1's
"a primary action exists" now also accepts a page that **declares** itself a reference surface
(`<meta name="wh-page-kind" content="reference">` — symbol-gallery, validator-catalog, design-system, architecture,
the llm-observability pointer): a declared contract can be audited, a heuristic cannot. Y1 honours the same declaration
(a reference doc loads supabase only for its founder gate and writes nothing). The board then grew again, 42 → 56: the
seeder serves subpath pages under `/workhive/`, so the 13 calculators + `learn/index` the P rows walk joined `PAGES`
(their only receipt had been the PROD load-level breadth); `critic_from_board.py --board <page.json>` banks a page run's
critiques without waiting for a full board. `stock-ripple`'s RED is the prover's UI-driven path: the
product's propagation was verified independently (psql-staged low → tile 3 → 4 → restored).

**Lessons that moved into the ruler and the tools:** an inline prose link is not a tap target; a repeated
row action is not a page CTA; a boot placeholder above the fold is two shifts, not one; a count read before
auth is a refusal, not an empty hive; the seeder must never regenerate over a row that has moved
(`seed_p_program_catalog.py` preserves moved rows verbatim); a lens that cannot apply to its surface is a
vacuous row (`LENS_SIGNALS`, asserted at build).

**Synthesis — rounds 1-5 of 2026-09-05, clustered by the job each finding does (the design judgment, not the list):**

1. **The instrument was wrong more often than the page (rows 6, 9, 10, 14, 28, 30, 41, 42, 43).** Nine "silent" pages were showing the platform's own fixed-position notice; two provers walked the seller profile without its query key; the SW prover navigated signed out; the rubric graded catalog cells as marketese. Verdict: FUSE the visibility, session and query-key preambles into ONE shared prover harness that every `prove_*.mjs` imports - today each prover carries its own copy and each copy grew a different blind spot. `tools/prover_harness.mjs` AUTHORED 2026-09-05 (SEEDER/HIVE/WORKER, signIn(ctx), PAGE_QUERY keyed by the page's own parameter, VIS_JS = checkVisibility, psql/psqlAs, SETTLE_MS); all nine provers wired and re-proved on it in chains 4-5 (degradation, hand-off, founder backfill, notice probe, SW identity, focus, backfill, fourth-state; claims in flight), its self-test registered as the fast gate `prover-harness-selftest` - DONE 2026-09-05. Blast radius: 9 prover files, no page. Owner: QA.
2. **Missing data was recorded as a ceiling (rows 45, 21, 27).** Sixteen "no second hive" rows were one seeder away. Verdict: the generators' n/a line now names its own fix ("missing DATA, not a ceiling: run tools/seed_second_hive_rows.py" - DONE 2026-09-05); the seeder stays in `tools/` beside the generators it serves - an n/a that names its own fix is a queue item, not a verdict.
3. **One central fix, several timing holes (rows 29, 44, 39, 23).** The transport settle ran too early; realtime pages never backfilled; the founder inbox class repeated on hive and community. Verdict: the backfill handler belongs in utils.js - DONE 2026-09-05: `whRealtimeBackfill(refetch, { tag })` (one instance per page, debounced across channels, refetches on 'online', exposes window._whRt); hive wired (community follows once the running chain releases it); the settle passes stay in utils. Keep distinct: the poll pages (alert-hub, platform-actions) - a 60 s poll IS the backfill and needs no handler.
4. **A cap that feeds a count (rows 8, 16, 26, 40).** Four founder tiles, the GCash badge, two 50-row badges. Verdict: the `reference-pages-uncapped` gate ALSO flags a count/badge painted from `.length` within the window after a capped read unless the read asks `count: 'exact'` or the line carries a `+` disclosure (DONE 2026-09-05, self-test bites on the GCash shape; 19 pages green) - the cap-ok annotation must name the consumer, and a badge is never rows-only.
5. **Rebuilding via innerHTML destroys the person's place (rows 46, 3, 13).** alert-hub and hive feeds, the marketplace svc pane before them. Verdict: one shared pair in utils.js - DONE 2026-09-05: `whFocusCapture(container)` before the first destructive step (a skeleton or a rebuild) and `whFocusRestore(container, cap)` after the last synchronous render (signature, then position, then first focusable; never steals focus the person moved); hive and alert-hub wired, the page-local IIFEs removed; the focus prover holds focus across the REAL tick for every polled feed in its roster.
6. **Lenses that do not apply were carried as debt (32 descoped today).** Platform-scoped surfaces, read-only pages, static posters, functions without an LLM call. Verdict: descope with the recorded reason is the honest state; the percentage is of in-scope rows and the reasons are auditable in the registry.
7. **A byte no diff can show (rows 44, 47, 48, 49, 51).** Four rewrites of the transport settle chased timing, isolation, repaint races and visibility; the cause was two backspace bytes where `` should have been, written through a heredoc, and the same byte sat in the rubric survey, a gate and the checks runner. Verdict: the class is PREVENTED by one fast gate (`no-control-bytes`, PASS over 2,933 code files, registered) and DIAGNOSED by one move - print the predicate's source from inside the runtime before theorising (`probe_hive_settle_trace.mjs`). Keep distinct: ANSI and unit-separator bytes in reporters and vendored code are program data, not mangled escapes - the gate targets only U+0008/0007/000B/0000.
8. **A critic wave closes per finding, never per row (rows 55-58).** The 339 'owed' critic rows were the rubric's own residual dimensions on the pages already fixed today; the honest close is `close_critic_findings.py` (a finding is clean when the page's CURRENT sweep no longer fails its dim; a row closes only when every finding is clean; partial rows print their remaining dims) driven by page-set sweeps, and the residuals fall in CLUSTERS that cross pages: sentences (B3), off-scale radii (S1), i18n keys and mechanism (N1), a filled primary action (A1), layout shifts (I1: the scrollbar gutter, reserves), silhouettes (R3), plus kind calibrations recorded in the rubric with their reason. Verdict: keep the closer strict (no bulk), sweep in sets of 8-14 pages, fix by cluster, re-sweep - the same loop the P-program used, one lens deeper. The 14 live-calculator rows are honestly blocked on promotion.
