## Platform finding · the writer that records what a walk discovered was destroying it (2026-09-10)

Found while looking for the psql-recipe template named in the bucket-1 NEXT queue. A bank finding read:

    "title": "V; A; L; U; E; D; O; E; S; N; O; T; S; U; R; V; I; V; E; T; H; I; S; S; E; A; M; ..."

`bank_page_walk.py` builds a finding title from a probe's notes:

```python
notes = [str(n) for n in (res.get("notes") or []) if str(n).strip()]
title = "; ".join(notes) if notes else ...
```

`notes` is normally a list. **When a probe hands back a single STRING, the comprehension iterates its
CHARACTERS** — and `if str(n).strip()` then discards every space, which is why the recovered text runs
together. Nothing raised and nothing was logged: a string is iterable, so Python did as it was told.

**43 findings across 16 bank files, 86 fields in total.** They are not decorations — de-separated, one
reads *"VALUE DOES NOT SURVIVE THIS SEAM — a real defect, so this row stays OWED rather than banked."*
Real defect reports, made unreadable by the instrument recording them, and invisible because the field
was still present, still a string, still roughly the right length. An unreadable finding is worse than
a missing one: a missing one is a gap somebody notices.

**Fixed at the writer** (`if isinstance(_notes, str): _notes = [_notes]`) — verified both ways: a list
still joins normally, and a string now yields `MEASURED AT THE EDGE` with its spaces intact.

**Repaired without fabricating.** Removing the separators restores the letters exactly; the spaces were
filtered out before the join and are gone for good. Word breaks were NOT guessed — each repaired field
carries a marker saying the spacing is missing, because inventing it would be fabricating the evidence a
second time. All 22 bank files still parse; `live-mcp-bank` re-run confirms *every non-owed row carries
typed, unexpired evidence*.

**The same exposure lives wherever `join()` meets an API that returns "a list or a string"** —
`bank_journey_run.py:88` does `"; ".join(row.get("problems"))` with the identical shape. Grep signature
for the damage: `^(?:[^;]; ){6,}`.

## Platform finding · FOUR banked database invariants had stopped being true (measured 2026-09-10)

`validate_psql_probe_suite` re-executes every recipe in `tools/psql_probes/`. It was **142/146**, and the
four reds were not flakes — each is an invariant a page bank still calls green.

**Three of them were one defect.** `seed_fleet_history.py` inserts inventory items with a literal opening
`qty_on_hand` (12, 6, 4, 8, 5) and wrote **nothing** to `inventory_transactions`. The job-consumption rows
added afterwards then computed their `qty_after` from a base of zero, so the shelf and its own ledger
described two different stock levels — nine items disagreeing, and `inventory__stock_conserved`,
`__movement_leaves_row` and `__no_negative_stock` all red on it. A one-sided ledger write: both halves
plausible alone, never reconciled, and nothing complained because nothing reads the pair together.

**The repair brought the LEDGER up to the shelf, not the reverse.** Pulling `qty_on_hand` down to the
ledger figure would have zeroed three Dela Cruz items and taken the spare-part journey (J23) straight back
to "nothing to move" — the exact gap that seeder exists to close. An `adjust` row recording the opening
stock is both true and useful, and `adjust` is one of the five words the product already uses.

**The cause is fixed, not just the data.** The seeder now writes a `receive` opening-balance row beside
every item it creates, so the shelf and its ledger start level — and `--revert` deletes those ledger rows
BEFORE the items, because a preservation rule on one side of a paired write is the shape this same file
already carries a scar from.

**The fourth was separate.** Five `wrench_chronicle` rows sat 1–2 levels above what their XP implies —
`current_level` written beside `xp_total` rather than derived from it. Recomputed to the product's own
curve (`level = max(n) where floor(100·n^1.8) ≤ xp`).

**Neither was mine, and that was checked rather than assumed.** The five were last touched at 14:55 by an
earlier seeding run; the three workers today's 7,987-row backfill DID touch at 20:42 — Rosa dela Cruz,
Oscar Ramos, Gloria Tan, the three fleet supervisors — came out exactly consistent with the same formula.
That is positive evidence the live XP trigger works and only the seeded rows bypassed it.

**Now 146/146, and the suite gained a recipe.** `skillmatrix__badge_uniqueness` converts the DB-provable
half of `one_submit_one_attempt`: the duplicate badge is refused with `23505` AND a control insert on a
free axis is accepted, so the refusal proves a working uniqueness rule rather than a table that rejects
everything. Zero probe residue.

**What it deliberately does NOT claim.** The oracle is "a double-submit creates neither a second attempt
nor a second badge", and only the badge half is enforced by the database: `skill_exam_attempts` has ZERO
unique or exclusion constraints and one trigger, `check_daily_row_cap(50/day)` — an abuse guard, not a
dedup. A double-submit past the client lock DOES create a second attempt row. That is arguably correct —
without an idempotency key the database cannot tell a double-submit from a legitimate retake — so the
recipe asserts the absence explicitly (`attempts_have_no_dedup_rule | t`) rather than implying coverage it
does not have, and the row keeps its live-walk evidence for the client half.

## Bucket-1 re-scoped · the queue said "≈10 rows, DB-provable" and TWO of them are not (2026-09-10)

Working the list rather than trusting it. Each item was checked against what the database actually
enforces before any recipe was written, because a psql recipe for a claim the schema does not hold is
a proxy assertion — the exact thing bucket 4 exists to refuse.

| # | item | what the database enforces | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `shift-brain/tenant_isolation` | RLS + policy | already `psql` — the template |
| 2 | `skillmatrix/one_submit_one_attempt` | badge: 2 unique indexes · **attempt: nothing** | **half** — badge converted, attempt stays live-walk |
| 3 | `voice-journal/double_submit_one_entry` | **nothing** — 0 unique constraints; its one trigger binds the submitter | **NOT convertible → bucket 4** |
| 5 | `shift-brain/plan_attributable` | 2 attribution columns on `shift_plans` | convertible |
| 8 | `alert-hub/dismissal_durable` | UNIQUE `(hive_id, alert_key)` | **converted ✓** |
| 9 | `public-feed/keyset_total_order` | `(created_at, id)` index present | convertible |
| 10 | `dayplanner/plan_links_not_duplicates` | 3 link columns on `schedule_items` | convertible |

**Two recipes written, both with teeth both directions and zero residue; the suite is 147/147.**

`alert-hub__dismissal_durable` answers the sibling oracle's own question from the index rather than
from the screen: the unique key is `(hive_id, alert_key)` with **no actor in it**, so one member
pressing Handled hides that alert from the entire hive. `dismissal_scope_stated` names that as the
failure mode — "one person quietly blinding the team" — so the DB half is settled and the remaining
half is whether the surface says so, which is a screen claim and stays live-walk.

**An instrument note worth keeping.** Item 8 was nearly written off: a query for a COLUMN named
`%dismiss%` returned zero across the whole schema. The enforcement lives in a TABLE — `alert_dismissals`
— and reading the cell's own evidence text ("upsert keyed onConflict 'hive_id,alert_key'") is what
found it. A schema question asked at the wrong granularity answers confidently and wrongly.

**Bucket-1 progress: FOUR recipes written, suite 145 → 149, all green, zero residue.**

| item | recipe | what makes its green mean something |
|---|---|---|
| 2 (half) | `skillmatrix__badge_uniqueness` | duplicate refused `23505` **and** a control on a free axis accepted |
| 8 | `alert-hub__dismissal_durable` | same teeth, plus the scope read from the INDEX not the screen |
| 9 | `public-feed__keyset_total_order` | a **naive cursor demonstrably loses a row** on the same manufactured tie |
| 10 | `dayplanner__plan_links_not_duplicates` | both detectors fire on a manufactured dangling ref and a manufactured reuse |

**Two of the four had NO live case to measure, and saying so is the point.** `community_posts` holds 116
posts with **zero** ties on `created_at`; `schedule_items` holds 231 rows with **zero** `logbook_ref`
set. Asserting "pagination never duplicates" over data with no tie, or "no dangling refs" over no refs,
is a green that proves the hard case never occurred — the vacuity this bank keeps re-learning. Both
recipes PRINT the empty population rather than hiding it, and manufacture the case inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK.

**And `dayplanner/plan_links_not_duplicates` is a forward LOCK, not an enforcement claim.**
`schedule_items.logbook_ref` has no foreign key — its only constraints are the primary key and an
auth_uid FK — so a dangling reference is possible by construction and "linked, not duplicated" is
application behaviour. The recipe locks the invariant and proves its detectors fire; it does not claim
the database prevents the violation, because it does not.

**Schema facts that each cost a draft, now recorded in the recipes so they are paid for once:**
`skill_badges.level` is an integer carrying `CHECK (1..5)` (so the control needs a different axis —
discipline); `schedule_items.id` is TEXT, NOT NULL, no default; `schedule_items.date` is TEXT, not a
date. Every one of them failed as a silent `MISSING` expectation, which looks exactly like a product
finding and is not.

## Platform finding · ONE AI route records which model answered; every other route records none (2026-09-10)

Surfaced by converting `shift-brain/plan_attributable`, whose oracle says *"a generated plan records
which orchestrator run, which inputs, which model — an AI write with no accountability record is the
AI6 class, and every write on this page is AI-authored."* Measured:

| route | traces | with a `model_chain` |
|---|---|---|
| `ai-gateway` | 20 | **20** |
| `ai-orchestrator` | 37 | **0** |
| `analytics-orchestrator` | 18 | **0** |
| `voice-transcribe` | 9 | **0** |
| `engineering-bom-sow` | 5 | **0** |
| `scheduled-agents` | 4 | **0** |
| `embed-entry`, `send-report-email` | 3 each | **0** |

**The mechanism works — `wh_traces.model_chain` is populated 20/20 on one route — and no other route
uses it.** So this is an ADOPTION gap, not a missing capability, which is the distinction that decides
whether it is a fix or a build.

**And it is expensive, measurably.** Eleven of the eighteen entries in the shared provider chain turned
out today to be model names their providers no longer serve — four Groq, all three Cerebras, one
Mistral, three OpenRouter — and every AI call had been walking four guaranteed 404s before one
answered. The single route that records *which model answered* is precisely the one that could have
said so, months earlier. An accountability record is not paperwork; it is the instrument that would
have caught the rot.

**For shift-brain specifically:** all 135 plans carry `generated_by` and `generated_at`, so WHAT and
WHEN are on every row. There is no model, no run id, no input manifest in the payload, and the planner
writes no `wh_traces` row at all. `shift-brain__plan_attributable` asserts each of those as facts — so
the day the planner starts recording a model, the recipe FAILS and someone updates the claim
deliberately rather than the gap closing unnoticed.

**A smaller finding inside it:** input-health provenance (`payload.degraded` + `payload.fetch_errors`)
is on 130 of 135 plans. Five lack it and only one of those is the test seed — so FOUR real orchestrator
plans record nothing about whether the reads they rest on succeeded. Ratcheted at ≤ 5 rather than
asserted true.

**An instrument note.** The first draft asserted input health was universal, because the key survey
used `SELECT DISTINCT jsonb_object_keys(payload)` across ALL plans — which returns the UNION of keys
and reads exactly like "every plan has these". Per-row counting is the only way to ask that question;
an aggregate over a set answers a different one.

| # | item | outcome |

| 1 | `shift-brain/tenant_isolation` | already `psql` — the template the rest follow |
| 2 | `skillmatrix/one_submit_one_attempt` | **half converted** — badge half provable, attempt half has no DB rule |
| 3 | `voice-journal/double_submit_one_entry` | **bucket 4** — zero unique constraints; its one trigger binds the submitter |
| 4 | `shift-brain/carry_count_true` | converted ✓ |
| 5 | `shift-brain/plan_attributable` | converted ✓ — and surfaced the model-accountability gap |
| 6 | `index/hive_deterministic` | converted ✓ |
| 7 | `hive/benchmark_aggregate_only` | converted ✓ |
| 8 | `alert-hub/dismissal_durable` | converted ✓ |
| 9 | `public-feed/keyset_total_order` | converted ✓ |
| 10 | `dayplanner/plan_links_not_duplicates` | converted ✓ as a forward LOCK (no FK exists to enforce it) |

**Every recipe proves its own control fails first.** A green that cannot go red is decoration, and four
of these had corpora that could not exercise their claim at all: 116 posts with zero `created_at` ties,
231 schedule items with zero `logbook_ref`, three multi-hive workers with zero `joined_at` ties, five
benchmark rows all at `sample_hives = 3`. Each prints its empty population and manufactures the case
inside `BEGIN/ROLLBACK` — the naive cursor demonstrably drops a row, `joined_at` alone demonstrably goes
ambiguous, the truncation and single-hive detectors demonstrably fire.

**Two findings the conversions produced that the rows themselves did not name:**

1. **`network_benchmarks` is structurally safe and that is not enough.** It carries no `hive_id`, so a
   column audit says "aggregate". But a row computed over ONE hive publishes that hive's private MTBF
   under a "network average" caption, and no schema check can see it — the leak is in the CARDINALITY.
   `sample_hives >= 2` is now locked, with teeth that catch k=1.

2. **`index/hive_deterministic` is deterministic by luck, not construction.** None of the three
   multi-hive workers has a `joined_at` tie today, so ordering by it alone happens to be stable. It
   stops being stable the moment two memberships are written in one transaction — exactly how an invite
   flow adding someone to two hives at once would do it. The recipe manufactures that tie and shows
   `(joined_at, hive_id)` surviving where `joined_at` does not.

**A false finding caught before it was filed.** `carry_forward` lengths cluster at 9–12 and then sit on
exactly 25 for ten plans, with nothing between 13 and 24 — the textbook signature of a write-time cap,
and all ten declare `caps.carry_forward = false`, which would have made the platform's own flag a lie.
It is not: Manila genuinely holds 25 open logbook entries, Lucena 12, Baguio 10. Three hives, three true
counts. The shape of a distribution is a hypothesis; the source table is the answer.

**NEXT: bucket 3 — the edge-function surface (~8 rows).** `assistant/bundle_hive_scoped`,
`pii_egress_rule`, `gateway_only_path`, `failure_renders_as_failure`, `project-report/regen_stable`,
`voice-journal/failed_transcribe_no_ghost`, `shift-brain` regeneration. Provable by INVOKING the
function rather than querying — a different harness, and `prove_fn_contracts.mjs` is the one that
already speaks it. Bucket 2 (~34 rows) stays in the walk lane; a psql recipe cannot see a rendered page.


## ★EXPANSION WAVE 4 — 2026-09-14: every page × every action × every layer, LIVED start to end (+5,760 rows, 3,959 → 9,719 in scope, 40.7% on seed day; re-seeded the same day without the 4 retired pages and with the board-routing rule)

> Ian, 2026-09-14: *"still there are AI sloppiness … overlapping and overflowing in using the platform through phone … journeys trajectories more deeper, start from the start to end for every page, such as in connection pages, where you have to search in the internet any files then upload it … not only the companion, it should be the whole nav-hub … just put the number of trajectories so that we won't be lost … expand and extend: we have to cover, explore, experience those uncovered, unexplored, and unexperienced layers."* And, on the instrument: *"it is still the same in the roadmap that we have to use strictly all the relevant MCPs to finish all the trajectories."*

**Why journeys, measured.** 118 of 119 public pages carried the full at-rest rubric and reported **6** overflow/overlap findings in total, while a person on a phone saw overlap. V1 excluded fixed/sticky chrome and the hub/companion shell as "by design", the rubric had **no occlusion check at all**, overflow was measured only at page level, only at rest, at 390, in English. The sloppiness lives in the states a journey passes through and in the layers a single-page survey never reaches. Ian's three words are the registry's own depths: **uncovered** = a (page, layer) cell with no row · **unexplored** = rows but none walked · **unexperienced** = walked once as a single-page check but never lived as a start-to-end journey.

### The number — measured by the seeder, printed with its arithmetic, never typed

`python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --dry-run` (2026-09-14):

| | per axis | × 3 axes |
|---|---:|---:|
| action stories — one start-to-end journey per distinct action a person can take on a served page: **root/app 271** (substrate page map `DB writes` as table.op + `RPC calls` + `Edge invokes`, each VERIFIED against the page's current source; + the upload on each of the 7 upload pages; + export/print where the page calls `window.print`; + on a page with no persisted action, one story per primary-styled control, min 1) · **learn 120** (the tool the guide is about · the sign-up line · its named calculator · a related guide, one per kind present, + the hub's 2) · **calculators 60** (search-arrival → worked example → compute → export/print → CTA) · **public-root 4** | **473** | 1,419 |
| nav-hub stories — the WHOLE shell (fab, panel, the 6 modes, global search, tiles, quick, companion, feedback, assist row, connectivity pill + detail, close), once per page whose source loads `nav-hub.js` | **32** | 96 |
| layer stories — 151 served pages × 13 layers = 1,963 cells; **295 lived** (a gated ≥4-page journey names the page AND the layer), **1,668 not** (926 uncovered + 742 unexperienced; 117 pages with no layer lived); minus **240** cells an action story on the same page already lives (an action IS its page's F story, a write IS its D story) | **1,480** | 4,440 |
| **new trajectories** | **1,921** | **5,760** |
| **design-lens stories (added 2026-09-15)** — one row per served page per applicable lens, kind `design`: root/app 32 × 7 (`slop`, `craft`, `audit`, `copy`, `motion`, `figma`, `critique`) · calculators 60 × 5 (no motion, no figma) · learn 55 × 4 (`slop`, `craft`, `audit`, `copy`) · public 4 × 4 — at phone-390 en, BOTH viewports (390 + 1280) in one batched round, so one axis per row | **760** | **760** (`W45839…W46598`) |
| confusion-ledger rows (running, `--add-confusions`) — C1…C28 minus the retracted C14, × 3 axes | | 81 |
| **wave 4 today** | | **6,601** rows · header **CLOSED 3,960 of 10,560 in scope · 37.5%** on 2026-09-15 |

Axes: phone-390 English · narrow-320 English · phone-390 Filipino. Wave code **W4**, ids `W41…W45790`, all `specced/5`; every row carries `axis {device, language}` and `w4 {kind, action | layer | host, fixture}` on the row itself, and `journey.pages == pages` (every row ≥ 4 pages). The critic bank grew by the same 5,760 (`critic_seed_missing.py`).

**The plan said 6,417 (433 + 1,706) × 3.** The seeder lands at 5,760 because (a) its action denominator is the *substrate-verified* item list rather than the plan-day judgement count (root 289 vs 268, learn 120 vs 69 — the plan's per-item exclusions were not written down and are not reproducible; the seeder's rules are), and (b) the plan itself said the layer figure "may land slightly under 1,706 — never over" once cells an action story already lives are removed (1,480). **The count is the seeder's count**; it is regenerated, not negotiated, and the header reads it.

### What every one of the 5,760 must be (SS-W4)

1. **Start to end.** Begins where a real person begins (`entry`: search-arrival, direct, hub-nav, email-push, qr-print, deep-link), reaches the page through the platform's own navigation (`_entry_chain` — a route, not a list), performs the action or provokes the layer, and **follows the effect to its terminus**: the row persisted (`RETURNING id`, reversed after), the record on the reader page (`readers(table)` measured from source), the alert, the mail, the credit, the limit message, the recovered queue. "The control was clickable" is never the end.
2. **Real inputs.** On the 7 upload pages the file is a **real file found on the internet** — integrations (a real CMMS / SAP-PM export or OEM manual), logbook (a nameplate / fault photo), inventory (a part photo), marketplace + marketplace-seller (listing photos), resume (a real maintenance-technician résumé), voice-journal (a real short clip played into the microphone) — downloaded once into `_fixtures/<kind>/` with `manifest.json` carrying its provenance (binaries gitignored, `_fixtures/` excluded from Vercel), uploaded in the journey and followed.
3. **Not one page.** Every journey crosses ≥ 4 pages (seeder-asserted: 5,760/5,760).
4. **The whole nav-hub** on each of its 32 host pages: `#wh-hub-fab` → `#wh-hub-panel` inside the viewport → each of the 6 `wh-hub-mode-btn` → `#wh-hub-global-search` (type, `#wh-hub-no-results`, pick a `#wh-hub-tiles` tile and arrive) → `#wh-hub-quick` → `#wh-hub-open-companion` (neither panel nor fab may cover the page's primary control; close returns focus) → `#wh-hub-open-feedback` → `#wh-hub-assist-row` → `#wh-hub-conn-pill` + `#wh-hub-conn-detail` with the offline queue count → close; every control announced in the page's language. Receipt: `--hub-controls 11`.
5. **Three axes, same story.**
6. **The overlap/occlusion record at every step**, inside the journey: after each step, at rest and after its interaction, `tools/phone_fit_audit.mjs` records **occlusion** (for every interactive control `document.elementFromPoint(centre)` must be the control or a descendant — a FAB, sticky header, consent bar, toast or hub/companion panel covering a control is a finding regardless of `position:fixed`, named with rect and z-index), **element overflow** (a child past its clipping parent; `scrollWidth > clientWidth` under hidden/clip with no ellipsis; an unbroken token wider than its container), **page overflow**, and the **state delta** (a finding that appears only after a step is tagged with that step). Findings bank as rubric dims — **V1 gained the occlusion branch (never by design)** and **R6 "Element overflow inside its container" is new** — and close through `close_critic_findings.py`, never by bulk.

7. **The design lens (2026-09-15).** Every served page is also seen through the installed design skills, each a row of its own: the page at phone-390 AND desktop-1280 in one batched round through the Playwright MCP (arrival as the person, the overlap record and the live measures — smallest visible font, text under 11/12 px, tap targets under 44, slow or ease-in motion, body measure, heading skips, horizontal spill — and a full-page screenshot at each), the lens's own playbook applied to that evidence, every finding fixed through Impeccable's craft floor and re-verified live, and the mechanical detector (`impeccable detect --json`) **clean on the page** before the row banks (`tools/bank_mcp_design_walk.py` runs it and refuses otherwise). Receipt: `--lens --viewports phone-390,desktop-1280 --detector <json>` plus `--scores` (audit, critique), `--languages en,fil` (copy), `--figma <fileKey> <nodes>` (figma). Gate `w4-design` re-scans every banked page on every run; `design-detector-ratchet` holds the platform-wide count.

### Order of walking (strictly through the MCPs — playwright for the surface, postgres for the effect, invoke + PostgREST-as-persona for a contract; serial on the 8 GB host; banked per row through `record_mcp_walk.py`)

nav-hub 32 (the chrome most likely to occlude; it loads on every app page) → the 7 upload pages (Ian's example: integrations → plant-connections → asset-hub → pm-scheduler) → root/app action stories by count descending (marketplace 30 → integrations 26 → hive 22 → marketplace-seller 21 → …) → root/app layer stories, LB / CI / H / RL first → calculators and articles at narrow-320, then Filipino, actions then layers. `--fast` at each page-batch close; the full board, commit, push, deploy are Ian's gates. **Cost:** ≈ 300 browser-hours at ~3 min per deeper, file-carrying, per-step-measured walk, across many sessions; the count is the count.

**The design lenses ride along (2026-09-15):** a page visited for any W4 walk gets its design rows in the same sitting, in the seeder's lens order — `slop → craft → audit → copy → motion → figma → critique` — mechanical lenses first so `critique` scores the fixed page and the Figma frame captures it. Root/app pages first (a fix in the shared chrome — `utils.js`, `nav-hub.js` — pays across all 32), then calculators, learn, public. Every fix batch: `impeccable context` once per session → `craft-floor.md` read → edit (whole-page discipline; a redesign-scale change is comped in Figma first) → `detect --json` clean on the edited files → `sw.js` bump per precached file + `validate_sw_shell_membership.py` → `design-detector-ratchet` green → re-verified live at both viewports → receipt → bank.

**The audit lens names BOTH browsers (2026-09-15, Ian: _"I thought we are using relevant live MCPs?"_).** The lens table above always said `Playwright + Chrome DevTools MCP` for `audit`, and the first three audit rows were banked on a Playwright probe alone. The ledger now enforces what the table said: `live_walk_manifest` routes every `^Design lens audit:` row to **`playwright-mcp + chrome-devtools-mcp`**, and a want containing a second `-mcp` half is satisfied only when BOTH halves are recognised in the basis — scoped to design rows, because applying it to wave 4's `Lived start to end` journeys would re-define thousands of already-earned rows and move the denominator 18 points, which is a scope change and not a repair. Two rows (W45841 achievements, W45848 ai-quality) reopened under the new rule and were re-earned the same day. What the second instrument buys, measured on a 4×-throttled phone over Slow 4G: the shared skeleton was a **non-composited** `background-position` animation that DevTools blamed for 0.024 of alert-hub's shift cluster, and the guide chip forced **113 ms of layout reflow** during load — 87 ms of it re-reading its own `position:fixed` rect, which nothing on the page can move. Neither is visible to a rendered-page probe. After the repair: 113 → 89 ms, that frame 87 → 6 ms, LCP 1046 → 718 ms, CLS 0.03 → 0.02. A new gate **`bilingual-t-arms`** joins the platform run: a `_t(en, fil)` whose two arms are byte-identical is a translation that can never happen, it passes every existing check, and Impeccable's critique found one I had written myself two hours earlier (floor 23, forward-only).

**Where the design lenses stand (measured from the registry, 23 of 760 rows banked across 4 pages).** achievements.html (6), ai-quality.html (6), alert-hub.html (6), analytics-report.html (5). Every one was walked live and holds under `w4-design`; the `figma` rows wait on the plugin's tools. What the lenses have actually bought, in the order they were found:

- **The instrument grew twice.** `tools/w4_design_audit.js` measures the five audit dimensions on the rendered page - focus rings by tabbing, layout shift attributed to the elements that caused it, 125% text, a reduced-motion pass, raw hex against `var(--)` - because scoring accessibility 0-4 from a screenshot is vibe, not measurement. Then the **Chrome DevTools MCP** joined the audit lens as its second instrument, and the ledger now refuses an audit receipt that names only one half. Two rows reopened under that rule the day it landed and were re-earned the same day.
- **Two shared-chrome defects only a trace could see.** The skeleton shimmer was a NON-COMPOSITED animation of `background-position-x` that DevTools blamed for 0.024 of alert-hub's layout-shift cluster; and the guide chip forced **113 ms of layout reflow** during load, 87 ms of it re-reading its own `position:fixed` rect, which nothing on the page can move. After: 113 -> 30 ms on the lightest page, that frame 87 -> 6 ms, LCP 1046 -> 718 ms, CLS 0.03 -> 0.02, all on a 4x-throttled phone over Slow 4G.
- **Two new gates, both forward-only.** `bilingual-t-arms` fails any NEW `_t(en, fil)` whose two arms are byte-identical - a translation that can never happen, invisible to every check the platform had, and Impeccable's critique found one written two hours earlier in the same session. `design-detector-ratchet` holds the per-antipattern floor.
- **A bounded exception with teeth.** analytics-report.html holds a dark app shell AND a white printed document in one file, so the detector pairs the shell's white text with the document's ground. A receipt may now carry findings a LIVE measurement disproves - but each is PINNED to its exact count with a reason, anything unclaimed still refuses the bank, and the gate AND `live_walk_manifest` re-check every count on every run. It proved itself the same day: a copy fix removed one pairing, the count fell 9 -> 8, and every affected row refused until the claim was re-measured.
- **The lens order matters and is kept.** `slop -> craft -> audit -> copy -> motion -> figma -> critique`, so the critique scores a page the mechanical lenses have already cleaned, and the Figma frame captures that page rather than the one that needed fixing.

- **The platform-wide TYPE FLOOR, swept and then GATED (2026-09-16).** Ranking every page by measured slop turned the design wave from "walk 760 rows one at a time" into "find the rule that is copied everywhere". The census found `undersized-ui-text` + `tiny-text` to be the largest REAL antipattern class once two artefact classes were set aside, and the fix was three tools rather than 143 page walks: **752 declarations lifted across 239 files**, taking the detector ratchet **943 -> 671 primary findings (-29%)**. index.html 99 -> 44, hive.html 55 -> 11, learn/index.html 59 -> 4. The strings were not decoration - index.html's four signed-in section headings sat at 9.92px ("Today at a Glance", "Quick Actions", "My Open Jobs", "All Tools"), its language switch at 10.56px, its readiness ladder at 9px - and one `.pill` rule copied BYTE-IDENTICALLY into 95 search-arrival pages held descriptive phrases at 10.4px uppercase (measured across the corpus: median 32 characters, 74% over 20, longest 44). New gate **`type-floor`** (`tools/fix_type_floor_sweep.py --check`, mutation-tested: a 9px declaration reddens it) is the SWEEPER in check mode, so the gate and the fix can never disagree about where the floor is.

- **Two false leads the census corrected first, and both are worth keeping.** (1) The first ranking put **583 of 943 findings on index.html** - 62% of the platform's slop on one page. The live detector said **99**. A substring filter on `"index.html"` had matched all 54 learn articles plus `about/` and `feedback/`: **180 files share that basename**. Acting on it would have meant rewriting the front door for defects living elsewhere, and leaving the 95-file template rule untouched. The tell was in the breakdown's SHAPE - dozens of repeated single-count pairs, which is what a corpus produces and a page does not. (2) **logbook.html's 101 and pm-scheduler.html's 31 are not slop at all**: both are `@media print`'s `color:#111` read against screen navy, **122 of the platform's 137 low-contrast findings**, with `#111` absent from either file's screen CSS. Every other low-contrast file has ZERO dark declarations inside a print block, so the remaining 15 are worth walking and these 122 are not. The sweeper therefore carries a `@media print` EXEMPTION that it REPORTS rather than applies silently (14 declarations today) - lifting a printed page's density would be the same category error in the other direction.

- **A glob that describes the common shape is not a glob that covers the set.** The sweeper's first run used `learn/*/index.html`, which walks straight past `learn/index.html` - the hub, and the single largest remaining file at 59 findings, all of them one 0.65rem rule painting 55 category chips. One line of coverage was worth 55 findings.

- **★THE PIN THAT ARGUED FROM THE CODE INSTEAD OF FROM THE RECORD (2026-09-16).** Ranking by class left `side-tab` as the largest open group, and I wrote five `.disproven.json` pins covering **183 findings**, each saying the same thing: a thick coloured `border-left` is "the platform's consistent vocabulary for a notice". `DESIGN.md` decides it in one sentence under Shapes - *"accent borders are 1 px tints of the status hue, NEVER a thick coloured `border-left`"* - and Impeccable's craft floor refuses the same construct from the other side, with its opening line already pointing at where to look: *"A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here."* I had never opened the record. **The error, named plainly: I argued from what the code DOES rather than from what the design record DECIDES, and consistency across 180 files is exactly what a drift looks like from the inside** - the more widespread a construct is, the more convincing that argument feels and the less it proves. All five pins are retracted IN PLACE (recorded, not deleted, so the mistake stays visible) and the construct is fixed: the learn articles' `.callout` and `.answer-first` (96 borders, 54 files) to a 1px tint of the same hue on all four sides, which is what DESIGN.md prescribes; utils.js's six shared builders, asset-hub's four and dayplanner's two to 1px, dropping only the thickness the rules object to. **A wrong pin is worse than an open finding**: an open finding is a question, a pin is an answer that nothing re-opens.

- **And the mirror-image discipline, needed within the hour.** One construct genuinely survived - `.prose-wh blockquote` on the 60 calculator pages - and it was re-pinned on the RULES' OWN WORDS rather than on how common it is: both rules enumerate the elements they govern and both name the same four (cards, list items, callouts, alerts), and a pull quote is none of them - no border-radius, no card, not interactive, and a left rule on a quotation is a typographic convention centuries older than the web. **Swinging from a self-serving pin to a blanket over-correction is the same failure wearing the other sign.** The tool that does the callout fix is selector-aware for a measured reason, not a stylistic one: `.answer-first` and `.prose-wh blockquote` carry the BYTE-IDENTICAL declaration `border-left: 3px solid #F7A21B`, so a plain string replace would have rewritten the one construct meant to survive - its self-test asserts that separation in a file holding both.

- **The sweep phase closed with the count halved and the remainder EXPLAINED.** Ratchet **943 -> 428**. More useful than the number: of what remains, the majority is pinned with a written mechanism rather than merely unexamined, and the live 30-host nav-hub walk came back **30/30 with zero findings** - the proof that a 143-file type-floor sweep and a platform-wide border change broke no layout, every control exercised, no control occluded at any step, focus returned. What is left is judgement work per page (glows, nested cards, gradient text), which is what the per-page design rows exist for.

- **★A LOADED TRAP FOUND WHILE RE-CENSUSING A GLOB: 60 STAGING PAGES THAT WOULD REVERT FIVE DAYS OF LIVE WORK (2026-09-16, NEEDS IAN'S DECISION).** Checking whether a sweep's glob had missed anything turned up `seo_assets/calc_pages_staging/`, whose generator says in its own header: *"STAGING, not the site root. Nothing ships until Ian reviews + moves it."* Measured: **all 60 staged pages have a served twin at `tools/<slug>/`, NONE is byte-identical, NONE is new, and all 60 are OLDER than the live page** - staged 2026-09-11, while the live copies have been maintained continuously since through the i18n pass, the contrast and tap-target fixes, the 12px type floor, the monospace unification and the callout-border correction. So "move staging to the site root" reads like shipping new work and would in fact **REVERT five days of fixes across 60 public pages, silently**, because a file copy leaves no diff to review. New gate **`calc-staging-not-stale`** makes it visible; it promotes and deletes nothing, because promotion is Ian's gate. **Its first version asked the wrong question and the mistake is kept in its header:** it compared MTIMES, which a re-run of the generator or any touch defeats - staging becomes newer while its CONTENT is still the old template, and the gate goes green with the trap intact. "Which file is older" was never the question; **"what would promoting this file UNDO"** is, and it is answerable from the bytes. The gate now asks the SWEEP TOOLS themselves what each staged page would reintroduce (rather than re-implementing their patterns and drifting from the fixers), and reports it: **180 sub-12px declarations, 120 thick callout borders, 60 kickers, 60 Windows-only mono stacks - 420 in all.** Its self-test touches the regressing page's timestamp to prove a refresh cannot clear it. **Two ways to clear it, both Ian's call and neither a touch of the timestamps: fix the GENERATOR (`tools/build_calc_pages.py`) so a rebuild is born correct, or delete the stale copies now their content has landed live.** This is the same shape as the dead cascading delete already in the bank - a path that looks like the normal next step and is destructive because the world moved under it while it sat there.

- **The dark-glow class, measured and split three ways instead of swept or dismissed (2026-09-16).** After the side-tab pin turned out to be wrong for arguing from how common the code was, the next-largest class got the opposite treatment: a measurement of what each shadow actually IS. Of **73 coloured box-shadows** on served pages - **14 are spread-only RINGS** (`0 0 0 2-3px rgba(hue,0.08-0.15)`), which DESIGN.md endorses in the very sentence that retires the glow (*"a tier is signalled by its ring colour and a 2px ring, NOT a glow"*), mostly focus rings, no action; **47 carry an offset AND a blur** (`0 8px 24px -4px rgba(247,162,27,0.45)` x27), so they meet the craft floor's depth bar and are NOT the decoration either rule names - but DESIGN.md's shadow vocabulary specifies BLACK at 16-34%, so an amber shadow under an amber CTA is outside the declared system while being good practice in general; **the record does not settle it, so it is Ian's decision rather than a sweep**; and **12 are genuine zero-offset blurred halos**, which is what DESIGN.md is retiring. Those 12 split again by what they DO: **8 status dots** (`.rag-dot`, `.presence-dot`, `.conn-dot`) where the dot's own fill already carries the state and the halo adds glow and no information - ordinary per-page work; **2 on dayplanner's now-marker**, where the glow is doing LEGIBILITY work on a 2px hairline laid over a busy 24-row grid and removing it may hide the one thing a supervisor scans for mid-shift - wants a live look first; and **2 in an `@keyframes` pulse** that animates unconditionally, which is two findings in one and fails the platform's existing pulsing-dot test (a pulse is legitimate only while it reports genuinely live, changing state). Full disposition: `.tmp/w4_design/dark-glow.disposition.json`.


### Verification

- Seeding: registry gate green; header **40.7% of 9,719**, `W4 5790/0/5790`, PAGE × LAYER at 295 lived of 1,963; the headline fell from 100% — the denominator moved.
- Per journey: ≥4 page transitions; the entry actually applied; every writing step's persisted effect returned and reversed; the real file's provenance in the manifest; the layer provoked and observed; the per-step record for every step at its axis's width and language — all enforced by `_w4_missing` (the ledger) and `record_mcp_walk.py` (the receipt).
- Blind-spot teeth: `rubric-teeth` green; `live_walk_manifest.py --check` shows zero W4 rows banked from a lens that cannot answer them.

### The confusion ledger — what confuses the walker confuses a person (Ian, 2026-09-14)

> *"even you sometimes confused like the sign in, that is why we have to have more trajectories, targeting that makes you confused, and work our way to improve it. it is the same way improving our UFAI UI UX platform wide"* — and, asked whether that meant sign-in: *"I am not referring to signing in only, I am referring to any other kinds and types."*

**`w4_confusions.json`** (repo root, tracked, append-only) is the ledger. Every point of ANY kind where a walk — an agent driving the platform as a person — hesitated, mis-clicked, picked the wrong control, waited without knowing, lost its place, hit a dead end, landed elsewhere than it meant to, or read a sentence it could not act on is written there the day it happens, with a **kind** from a fixed taxonomy (`ambiguity`, `wait-without-knowing`, `unactionable-sentence`, `silent-scope`, `lost-place`, `look-alike-controls`, `silent-failure`, `dead-end`, `wrong-arrival`, `hidden-by-chrome`, `chrome-stands-down`, `off-screen` — added 2026-09-14 for C17: a control clipped by the viewport edge, hidden by no chrome; `wrapped-label` — added 2026-09-14 for C19: a one-line control's label breaking onto two lines at a narrow width), the page, the walk that met it, and the improvement it must live. `python tools/seed_expansion_wave4.py --add-confusions` turns each entry into **one W4 row per axis** (kind `confusion`, `w4.confusion = C<n>`), lived start to end on the page where it was met; entries already seeded are skipped so the ledger can grow and the command re-run. Two kinds are also **measured automatically on every step** by `tools/phone_fit_audit.mjs`: `ambiguity` (visible controls of one role sharing a name inside one landmark) and `unactionable` (a visible alert carrying the transport's words); the walk reads the rest.

**First entries (from W41366, the first walk):** C1 two "Sign In"s on the wall (ambiguity) · C2 25 s of "Signing in…" with nothing said (wait-without-knowing) · C3 "name resolution failed" shown to the person (unactionable-sentence) · C4 the tools filter silently scoped to the current mode (silent-scope) · C5 focus on `<body>` after every close (lost-place) · C6 a search button and a filter input that look alike (look-alike-controls) · C7 `_tt is not defined` on every mode click (silent-failure). Seeded as **W45764–W45784** (+21, 9,743 in scope, 40.6%). Later the same day the ledger grew to 17 entries and every un-retracted one is a row per axis: C11–C13 + C15 as **W45791–W45802** (C14 was RETRACTED — a walk artifact, the hub standing down behind the sign-in dialog by design — and the seeder now skips a `retract`ed entry), C16–C17 as **W45803–W45808** (found by the first narrow-320 walk that could sign in, once a wedged Docker host mount was recovered: hive's tile snooze under the hub FAB; assistant's "New Chat" 21 px past the viewport, the new `off-screen` kind). Each confusion row is lived again by **`tools/prove_w4_confusions.mjs`** (gate `w4-confusions`): the row's worker walks the row's path on the real page at the axis and a per-confusion predicate reads whether the improvement holds — a predicate that fails keeps its row open. **★RETRACTED 2026-09-15 07:30 — the instrument was wrong.** Everything the next two paragraphs describe as "banked" was walked by node / python prover scripts (`tools/prove_w4_*`), not through the MCPs the plan names as the instrument ("walk every one strictly through the relevant MCPs … no headless library batching", Ian 2026-09-14). Ian: *"I thought we are using relevant live MCPs for this roadmap?"* All 4,515 prover-banked W4 rows were reverted to specced with the retraction in their basis; the product fixes, the receipts and the provers (as board gates) stand; every row is re-earned through the MCP walk, per row, from here. The paragraphs are kept as the record of what the scripts found. **First results (2026-09-14 evening, library walks): all 32 English confusion rows lived clean and were banked** (16 at phone-390, 16 at narrow-320, gates `w4-confusions` / `w4-confusions-320-en`) — after the prover found three things the bank had missed and they were fixed at source: at 390 the consent card (z 9000) sat ON the open sign-in dialog's SSO / Create buttons (the first C13 fix had only reflowed ≤360 and its comment *assumed* "behind the modal"; now a `:has(#signin-modal:not(.hidden))` rule stands it down at every width), hive's tile snooze under the hub FAB at 320 (C16), assistant's "New Chat" 21 px past the 320 viewport (C17). Six other "still confusing" verdicts were instrument faults, each corrected in the prover rather than argued away: a nonsense filter term where the story needs a tool hidden by the view, a `display:none` back-link, predicates run on a page that lacks the control (`on:` binds each to its page), an offline banner measured mid-transition (6 px), a FAB-column rule applied at 390, and quick tiles inside the closed hub panel read as covered. **The narrow-320 nav-hub axis then ran to completion (2026-09-14 night, serial, preflighted): 22 light hosts walked, 17 clean on the first pass, the other 5 each a genuine 320 finding fixed at source and re-walked clean** — community's filter chips under BOTH FABs (C18, the chip block now reserves both columns below 360), analytics-report's tabs wrapping (C19) and its BETA badge off-screen (C23), report-sender's Install button 62 px off-screen (C20, sw v391), resume's paired upload buttons wrapping (C21), voice-journal's "Speak again" wrapping (C22) — six more ledger entries, each seeded as rows and lived by the prover. The Filipino axis followed the same night (23/23 light hosts; the 22 confusions all lived clean in Filipino - "Nagsa-sign in pa…", "Pansamantalang hindi available ang pag-sign in", "Walang Engineer na tool na tumugma. Ipakita ang lahat ng tools"), and the seven "heavy" hosts turned out to walk fine once their cast accounts were addressable and the Docker mount had been recovered — **the nav-hub family closed at 90/90 on 2026-09-15 00:18**, after two more findings on the way: index.html as a signed-in host had its navigation hidden at every width because the consent card carried `role="dialog"` (the hub stands down for any open dialog; the card is now a `region`, and reflows in-flow at every width — C25), and shift-brain's "Publish to crew" wrapped at 320 (C26). The action rows followed overnight with `tools/prove_w4_actions.mjs`, which walks each (path, cast) group once and answers every row from what the person's own session received: **every learn-cta row at phone-390 (119/119) lived clean** once the prover resolved all five CTA shapes the seeder emits (named tool, named calculator, related guide, the sign-up line, open-workhive), the rpc rows the pages call at load or that the person's session can call with its own context (hive, worker, a 30-day window) banked, and the rows that need a hand stayed open by design — a MUTATING rpc is never called by a walk (the first build called `deactivate_my_account` as the cast, deactivated two local accounts, and banked both as "lived clean"; repaired within the hour, the deny-list is the rule now), an edge function that only a page control invokes, a `cta` label hidden until a calculator is chosen, a form, a file, a computation. Found on the way: **C24** (the wall silently normalises usernames to `[a-z0-9_]`, so three seeded accounts could never sign in and read "Wrong username or password" — renamed; the wall now shows the handle it will use), **C25** (the consent card carried `role="dialog"`, and the hub stands down for any open dialog, so the signed-in landing page had no navigation at any width until the card was answered — a region now, in-flow everywhere), **C26** (shift-brain's "Publish to crew" wrapped at 320), **C27** (all sixty calculator guides send `?calc=<slug>` and engineering-design never read it — it does now). C4/C5/C7 fixed and verified live the same day; C1–C3 fixed on the wall (inert page behind the dialog; a still-trying hint at 8 s; plain copy for a 5xx with the raw text to the error log) and verified with the login call stubbed through CDP (the service worker issues the page's requests, so `page.route` alone never sees them).
